These are the appointed times of the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations. These are my appointed times:
23.3: On six days work may be done, but on the seventh day there shall be a sabbath of complete rest, a holy convocation. You shall not do any work. It shall be a sabbath to the Lord in all the places you live.
23.4: These are the appointed times of the Lord, the holy convocations which you shall proclaim at their appointed times.
23.5: The first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight, is the Lord’s Passover,
23.6: and the fifteenth day of this month is the Festival of Unleavened Bread for the Lord. You shall eat unleavened bread for seven days.
23.7: On the first day a holy convocation is to be proclaimed for you. You shall not do any work in your regular occupation.
23.8: You shall present an offering by fire to the Lord for seven days. The seventh day shall be proclaimed as a holy convocation. You shall not do any work for your regular occupation.
23.10:
to speak to the people of Israel and tell them this:
When you enter the land that I am giving to you and you reap its harvest, and when you bring the first sheaf of your harvest to the priest
23.11: so that he may wave the sheaf before the Lord so that you will be accepted, the priest shall wave it on the day after the Sabbath.
23.12: On the day that you wave the sheaf, you shall offer as a burnt offering to the Lord a lamb without blemish, one year old.
23.13: The grain offering accompanying it is to be four quarts of fine wheat flour mixed with oil, a gift to the Lord, a pleasing aroma. The drink offering accompanying it shall be a quart of wine.
23.14: You shall not eat any of this year’s bread or roasted grain or fresh ears until this very day, until you have brought the offering of your God. This is a permanent regulation throughout your generations in all the places you live.
23.15: Then from the day after the Sabbath, from the day that you bring the sheaf to be waved, you shall count off seven weeks for yourselves. They must be complete weeks.
23.16: You shall count fifty days, until you reach the day after the seventh Sabbath. Then you shall present an offering of new grain to the Lord.
23.17: From the places where you live you shall bring two loaves of bread as a wave offering. They shall be made of four quarts of fine wheat flour, baked with yeast, as first ripe produce for the Lord.
23.18: Then with the bread you shall present seven lambs without blemish, each of them one year old, one young bull from the herd, and two rams—they shall be a whole burnt offering for the Lord, together with their grain offerings and their drink offerings, an offering made by fire, with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
23.19: You shall also present the sin offering with one male goat and the fellowship offering with two one-year-old male lambs.
23.20: The priest shall wave them, together with the bread from the first ripe produce, as a wave offering before the Lord, in addition to the two lambs. They shall be holy to the Lord for the priest.
23.21: On this very same day you shall make a proclamation. A holy convocation will be proclaimed for you. You shall do no work in your regular occupation. This is a permanent regulation in all the places you live throughout your generations.
23.22: When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not completely reap the edges of your field or gather the dropped stalks from your harvest. You shall leave them for the poor and for the resident alien. I am the Lord your God.
23.24:
to speak to the people of Israel:
In the seventh month, on the first of the month, you shall have a complete rest, a memorial celebration with loud blasts of the ram’s horn, proclaimed as a holy convocation.
23.25: You shall not do any work in your regular occupation, and you shall present a gift made by fire to the Lord.
23.27: It is the tenth day of this seventh month that is the Day of Atonement. It shall be proclaimed as a holy convocation for you. You shall humble yourselves, and you shall present an offering made by fire to the Lord.
23.28: You shall not do any work on this special day, because it is the Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the Lord your God.
23.29: Indeed, anyone who does not humble himself on this special day will be cut off from his people.
23.30: Anyone who does any work on this very special day, I will exterminate from the midst of his people.
23.31: You shall do no work. This is a permanent regulation throughout your generations in all your places where you live.
23.32: It is a sabbath of complete rest for you. You shall humble yourselves on the ninth day of the month at evening. From that evening until the next evening, you shall observe a sabbath rest.
23.34:
to tell the people of Israel this:
Beginning on the fifteenth day of this seventh month, celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days for the Lord.
23.35: On the first day proclaim a holy convocation. You shall not do any work for your regular occupation.
23.36: For seven days you shall bring an offering made by fire to the Lord. On the eighth day proclaim a holy convocation for yourselves, and you shall present an offering made by fire to the Lord. This is a closing ceremony. You shall not do any work for your regular occupation.
23.37: These are the appointed times of the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations for the presentation of offerings made by fire to the Lord—burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings as commanded for each day.
23.38: Offer these in addition to the Sabbath offerings of the Lord, in addition to your personal wave offerings, in addition to all your offerings to fulfill a vow, and in addition to all your voluntary offerings that you give to the Lord.
23.39: Beginning exactly on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, when you go to celebrate the festival of the Lord for seven days as a pilgrim, there shall be a complete sabbath rest on the first day and a complete sabbath rest on the eighth day.
23.40: On the first day you shall select for yourselves fruit from splendid trees, branches of palm trees, boughs from leafy trees, and willows from by the stream—and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God for seven days.
23.41: Celebrate the festival for the Lord as a pilgrim for seven days each year. This is a permanent regulation throughout your generations. In the seventh month you shall celebrate the festival as a pilgrim.
23.42: You shall live in temporary shelters for seven days—every native-born person in Israel shall live in shelters—
23.43: so that your generations may know that I made the people of Israel live in shelters when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
23.44: That is what Moses said about the appointed times of the Lord to the people of Israel.

24.1: The Lord spoke to Moses:
24.2: Command the Israelites to bring you clear oil from beaten olives for the Light so the lamps will be kept burning continually.
24.3: Aaron shall set the Light before the Lord in the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil which is in front of the Testimony, every night from the evening to the morning. It is a permanent regulation throughout your generations.
24.4: He shall set the lamps regularly on the pure gold lampstand before the Lord.
24.5: You shall take fine flour and bake twelve round loaves from it. Each loaf shall be made with four quarts of flour.
24.6: You shall put them in two stacks, six to each stack, on the pure gold table before the Lord.
24.7: Upon the stacks you shall place clear frankincense as a memorial portion for the bread. It is a gift of food to the Lord.
24.8: On every Sabbath day he shall arrange it before the Lord regularly. It is a permanent covenant on behalf of the Israelites.
24.9: The bread shall belong to Aaron and his sons, who shall eat it in a holy place, for it belongs to him as a most holy thing from the gifts of food to the Lord, a perpetual allotment.
24.10: A man who was the son of an Israelite woman and of an Egyptian man came along with the Israelites. This son of the Israelite woman fought with another Israelite in the camp.
24.11: The Israelite woman’s son blasphemed the Name and cursed, so they brought him to Moses. (His mother’s name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, belonging to the tribe of Dan.)
24.12: They put him in custody to wait for a decision from the mouth of the Lord.
24.13: Then the Lord spoke to Moses:
24.14: “Take the man who cursed outside the camp, and all those who heard it shall lay their hands on his head, and the whole community shall stone him.
24.15: Then speak to the Israelites: If anyone curses his God, he shall bear his sin,
24.16: but if anyone blasphemes the name of the Lord, he must certainly be put to death; the whole community must stone him. Whether he is an alien or a citizen, when he has blasphemed the Name, he must be put to death.”
24.17: “If anyone hits someone and kills him, he must certainly be put to death.
24.18: But one who strikes and kills an animal must make restitution for it, a life for a life.
24.19: If anyone injures his fellow citizen, he shall have the same thing done to him as he has done:
24.20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As he injured that other person, the same is to be done to him.
24.21: One who strikes an animal so that it dies shall make restitution for it, but one who strikes a human being and kills him shall be put to death.
24.22: You shall have the same standard of justice for the alien who lives with you and for the citizen, for I am the Lord your God.”
24.23: After Moses had spoken this to the Israelites, the man who had cursed was taken outside the camp and stoned to death. The Israelites did as the Lord had commanded Moses.

25.1: The Lord spoke to Moses at Mount Sinai,
25.2:
“Speak to the Israelites and say this to them.”
When you enter the land that I am giving to you, the land shall observe a sabbath rest for the Lord.
25.3: For six years you may sow your field, and for six years you may prune your vineyard and gather its produce.
25.4: But in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath of complete rest for the land, a sabbath for the Lord. You shall not sow your field, and you shall not prune your vineyard.
25.5: You shall not reap the produce that grows by itself from your harvest or gather the grapes from your unpruned vine. It shall be a year of complete rest for the land.
25.6: The sabbath of the land will, however, provide food for you—for you, for your male slaves and for your female slaves, for your hired workers and for your servants who are living with you temporarily as aliens working for you,
25.7: for your livestock and for the wild animals which are in your land. You may eat all its produce.
25.8: You shall count off seven weeks of years. Count off seven years seven times, so that the duration of the seven weeks of years is forty-nine years.
25.9: Then you shall sound loud blasts on the ram’s horn. In the seventh month on the tenth day, on the Day of Atonement, you are to have a ram’s horn sounded throughout your land,
25.10: so that you may set aside the fiftieth year as holy and proclaim liberty throughout the land for all its inhabitants. It shall be a Jubilee for you, so that each of you may return to his family property and each of you may return to his clan.
25.11: The fiftieth year shall be a Jubilee for you. You shall not sow the field, and you shall not reap the grain that grows by itself, and you shall not gather fruit from its unpruned vines.
25.12: Because it is a Jubilee, it shall be holy for you. You may eat its produce from the field.
25.13: In this year of Jubilee each of you shall return to his family property.
25.14: When you sell some land to your countryman, or when you buy land from your countryman, you must not cheat your brother Israelite.
25.15: When you buy from your countryman, set the price according to the number of years since the last Jubilee. When he sells it to you, he shall set the price according to the number of years of produce left till the next Jubilee.
25.16: When there are many years left, you shall increase the purchase price. When there are few years left, you shall decrease its purchase price, because what the owner is actually selling to you is the amount of produce.
25.17: So each of you must not cheat your countryman, but you shall fear your God, for I am the Lord your God.
25.18: You shall carry out my regulations, and you shall observe my ordinances. You shall carry them out, so that you may live on the land securely.
25.19: The land will yield its fruit, and you will eat your fill and live securely on it.
25.20: If you ask, “What will we eat during the seventh year, since we may not sow and we may not gather our produce?”
25.21: I will command my blessing for you in the sixth year, so that the land will yield enough produce for three years.
25.22: When you sow in the eighth year, you will still be eating from the sixth year’s crop. You will eat the sixth year’s crop until the ninth year, when its produce comes in.
25.23: But the land must not be sold without a right to recover it, for the land really belongs to me. You are actually resident aliens under my authority.
25.24: Therefore, throughout all the land that you possess, you shall grant the right of redemption for the land.
25.25: When your brother Israelite becomes so impoverished that he has to sell some of the land that he holds, his closest relative shall come and redeem what his brother has sold.
25.26: When the man who has no close relative prospers and acquires enough for the price to redeem his land,
25.27: he may calculate the years since he sold it, refund the difference to the man to whom he sold it, and return to his family property.
25.28: But if he does not acquire a sufficient amount to recover the land for himself, what he has sold shall remain under the control of the one who bought it until the year of Jubilee. It shall become free in the Jubilee, so that the seller may return to his family property.
25.29: When a man sells a house where he lives in a walled town, his right of redemption shall last until a full year after its sale. The time to redeem it lasts for a year.
25.30: But if it is not redeemed before the completion of a full year, the house which is in a town which has a wall will belong to its buyer and his descendants. It cannot be reclaimed. It will not be released in the Jubilee.
25.31: But the houses in the villages that have no wall around them shall be classified as part of the farmland. They have the right of redemption and shall become free in the Jubilee.
25.32: All the towns of the Levites and the houses in the towns which are their property have a permanent right of redemption.
25.33: Whatever a Levite is permitted to redeem (such as a house which he sold that had been his property in a city) will become free in the Jubilee, because the houses in the towns of the Levites are their possession among the Israelites.
25.34: But the pastures and fields around the Levites’ towns may not be sold, for that is their permanent possession.
25.35: When your fellow Israelite becomes so impoverished that he cannot support himself, help him as you would help a resident alien or a temporary resident. Let him retain his right to work for a livelihood among you.
25.36: You shall not take advance interest or accrued interest from him, but you shall fear your God and let your brother retain his livelihood with you.
25.37: You shall not lend him your money for advance interest or your food for accrued interest.
25.38: I am the Lord your God, who freed you from the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
25.39: When your fellow Israelite becomes so indebted to you that he is sold to you, you shall not make him serve as a slave.
25.40: He shall remain with you as a hired laborer or a temporary resident. He shall work for you until the year of Jubilee.
25.41: Then he and his children with him will become free from your authority. He shall return to his family home and to his ancestral landholding,
25.42: for the Israelites are my servants, whom I freed from the land of Egypt. They shall not be sold in a slave sale.
25.43: You shall not rule over them harshly, but you shall fear your God.
25.44: You may buy a male slave or a female slave for yourself from the nations around you.
25.45: You may also buy some of the children of those who reside as aliens among you and some of their extended families who are born in your land, so that they become your property.
25.46: You may leave them to your children as inherited property. You may make them work as slaves for life. But as for your brothers, the Israelites, each of you must not rule over your brother harshly.
25.47: If a resident alien living among you prospers, and if your brother Israelite becomes so indebted to him that he is sold to that alien living among you or to that alien’s family,
25.48: the Israelite who has been sold shall have the right to be redeemed. One of his brothers may redeem him,
25.49: or his uncle or his cousin may redeem him, or anyone from his immediate family or extended family may redeem him, or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.
25.50: Together with his buyer, he shall calculate the elapsed time from the year that he was sold until the year of Jubilee, and the price to redeem him shall be based on that number of years. It shall be calculated as if he were a hired laborer.
25.51: If there are still many years left, he shall pay the price of redemption proportionally to the years that have passed.
25.52: If only a few years remain until the year of Jubilee, he shall calculate the redemption in this way: He shall pay the price of his redemption on the basis of his years of work,
25.53: as if he were a worker hired year by year. You shall see to it that the owner does not rule over him harshly.
25.54: If he has not been redeemed in any of these ways, he and his children with him shall become free in the year of Jubilee,
25.55: because the Israelites are servants who really belong to me. They are my servants whom I freed from the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.

26.1: You shall not make gods that are really not gods for yourselves, and you shall not set up an image or a sacred memorial stone for yourselves, and you shall not set up a carved stone relief in your land to bow down to it, for I am the Lord your God.
26.2: You shall observe my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the Lord.
26.3: If you walk according to my regulations and keep my commandments and carry them out,
26.4: I will give you rains in their season, so that the land will yield its produce and the trees in the farmland will yield their fruit.
26.5: Threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will last until the time for sowing. You will eat your food until you are full, and you will live securely in your land.
26.6: I will give peace in the land so that you may lie down without anyone frightening you. I will eliminate ferocious animals from the land, and no sword will pass through your land.
26.7: You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
26.8: Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand, and your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
26.9: I will look on you with favor, and I will make you fruitful and will multiply you, and I will keep my covenant with you.
26.10: You will eat grain from previous harvests, grain long stored, until you remove the old grain to make room for the new.
26.11: I will place my Dwelling in your midst, and I will not at all detest you.
26.12: I will walk about in your midst, and I will be your God, and you will be my people.
26.13: I am the Lord your God, who freed you from the land of Egypt so that you would not be slaves to them. I broke the bars of your yoke so that I could make you walk upright.
26.14: But if you will not listen to me and do not obey all these commandments,
26.15: if you reject my regulations and you detest my ordinances so much that you do not obey all my commandments, so that you break my covenant,
26.16: I in turn will do this to you: I will inflict upon you panic, wasting disease, and fever, which will cause your eyes to fail and your vitality to slip away. You will sow your seed but get no return, for your enemies will eat it.
26.17: I will set my face against you. You will be beaten by your enemies, and those who hate you will rule over you. You will flee, even though nobody is pursuing you.
26.18: If, despite these things, you will not listen to me, I will go on to discipline you seven times for your sins.
26.19: I will break your proud strength and make your sky like iron and your land as hard as bronze,
26.20: so that your strength will be exhausted without accomplishing anything. Your land will not yield its produce, and the trees on the land will not yield their fruit.
26.21: If you still remain hostile to me and you are not willing to listen to me, I will multiply the plague against you seven times more according to your sins.
26.22: I will send against you the wild animals so that they will deprive you of your children and cut off your livestock. They will make you so few that your roads will be deserted.
26.23: If in spite of all these things you still refuse to be disciplined by me, and you remain hostile to me,
26.24: I will also remain hostile to you. I will strike you seven times more for your sins.
26.25: I will bring a sword on you to avenge the covenant. If you withdraw into your towns, I will send an epidemic among you, so that you will be delivered into the hand of the enemy.
26.26: When I break your supply of bread, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven. They will have to ration your bread, and though you eat, you will not be satisfied.
26.27: But if, in spite of all this, you will not listen to me and remain hostile to me,
26.28: I will remain hostile to you in anger. I myself will discipline you seven times as much for your sins.
26.29: You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.
26.30: I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense burners, and place your corpses on the corpses of your filthy idols. With all my heart I will detest you.
26.31: I will turn your towns into a wasteland and make your holy places desolate, and I will not smell the pleasing aroma of your sacrifices.
26.32: I myself will make your land so desolate that your enemies who settle in it will be appalled at it,
26.33: while I scatter you among the nations and unsheathe my sword against you. Then your land will be a desolation, and your towns will be a wasteland.
26.34: The land will then enjoy its sabbaths during all the days of its desolation, while you are in the land of your enemies. Yes, the land will rest and enjoy its sabbaths.
26.35: All the days when it is desolate it will rest, because it did not rest on your sabbaths when you lived there.
26.36: As for those of you who survive, I will bring despair into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, so that the sound of a scattered leaf will scare them away. They will flee as though fleeing from a sword, and they will fall though no one is pursuing them.
26.37: Each of them will stumble over his brother, as if from a sword, even though no one is pursuing him. You will have no power to stand against your enemies,
26.38: and you will perish among the nations. The land of your enemies will devour you.
26.39: Those of you who survive will rot away in the lands of your enemies because of their guilt. They will rot away because of the guilt of their ancestors.
26.40: They will confess their guilt and the guilt of their ancestors because of the unfaithfulness that they committed against me, and also because they remained hostile to me.
26.41: So I in turn became hostile to them, and I brought them into the land of their enemies. So their uncircumcised hearts will then be humbled, and they will then accept the punishment for their guilt.
26.42: Then I will remember my covenant with Jacob. I will remember also my covenant with Isaac and my covenant with Abraham as well. I will remember the land.
26.43: The land will be empty of them, so that in its desolation it may enjoy its sabbaths without them, while they suffer punishment for their guilt, because, and only because, they rejected my ordinances and they detested my statutes with all their heart.
26.44: Yet, for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, and I will not detest them so much that I exterminate them. I will not annul my covenant with them, for I am the Lord their God.
26.45: I will remember in their favor the covenant to be their God that I made with their first generation, whom I freed from the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations. I am the Lord.
26.46: These are the regulations, the ordinances, and the laws that the Lord instituted between himself and the people of Israel at Mount Sinai through Moses.

27.2:
“Speak to the Israelites and say this to them.”
When a person makes a special vow to the Lord which is based on the value of different classes of people,
27.3: the set value of a male from twenty years to sixty years of age is fifty shekels of silver, using the sanctuary shekel as the standard.
27.4: If it is a female, the value is thirty shekels.
27.5: If the age is from five years to twenty years, the value is twenty shekels for a male and ten shekels for a female.
27.6: If the age is from one month to five years, the value for the male is five shekels of silver, while the value for the female is three shekels of silver.
27.7: If the age is sixty years or over, the value is fifteen shekels for a male and ten shekels for a female.
27.8: But if anyone making a dedication is too poor to pay that standard value, he shall appear before the priest with the dedicated person, and the priest shall assess a substitute valuation for the person. The priest shall assess a value on the basis of what the person who has made the vow can afford.
27.9: If what is vowed is livestock which is acceptable as an offering to the Lord, anything that a person dedicates to the Lord is set apart as holy.
27.10: He may not exchange it or substitute another for it, either good for bad, or bad for good. If he substitutes one animal for another, both the animal and its substitute are set aside as holy.
27.11: If what has been vowed is any kind of unclean livestock, which may not be presented as an offering to the Lord, he shall present the animal before the priest
27.12: so that the priest may assess it. Whatever value is set by the priest, whether high or low, will be binding.
27.13: But if he does indeed redeem it, he must add one-fifth to its value.
27.14: When a person dedicates his house as holy to the Lord, the priest shall assess it. Whatever value the priest assesses, whether high or low, will be binding.
27.15: But if the person who has dedicated his house redeems it, he must add one-fifth to its value in silver, so that it belongs to him again.
27.16: If a person dedicates any field from his family property to the Lord, its value shall be based on how much seed is needed to sow it. Land sown by six bushels of barley seed is worth fifty shekels of silver.
27.17: If he dedicates his field during the year of Jubilee, its value stands as stated,
27.18: but if he dedicates his field after the Jubilee, the priest shall recalculate its value in silver based on the number of years that are left until the next year of Jubilee, and that much will be deducted from the value.
27.19: If the person who dedicated the field redeems it, he must add one-fifth to its value in silver, so that it may be returned to him.
27.20: But if he does not redeem the field but has sold the field to another person, it may no longer be redeemed.
27.21: When the field is released on the Jubilee, it will be set aside as holy. It belongs to the Lord as a dedicated field. It belongs to the priest as his holding.
27.22: If someone dedicates to the Lord a field he has purchased that is not part of his family landholding,
27.23: the priest shall calculate the amount of value until the year of Jubilee, so that he may pay the value on that day as something holy to the Lord.
27.24: In the year of Jubilee, the field shall return to the person from whom the donor bought it, to the one to whom the landholding originally belonged.
27.25: Every value shall be based on the sanctuary shekel, which has twenty gerahs to the shekel.
27.26: However, no one may dedicate a firstborn from the livestock that has already been designated for the Lord as a firstborn, whether it is a head of cattle or a sheep or a goat. It already belongs to the Lord.
27.27: But if it is one of the unclean livestock, he may buy it back at its set value plus one-fifth. If it is not redeemed, it may be sold at its set value.
27.28: However, if anyone devotes anything that belongs to him to the Lord unconditionally, whether it is a human being or livestock or any part of his landholding, it may not be sold and may not be redeemed. Everything devoted unconditionally is most holy to the Lord.
27.29: Any person who has been devoted to destruction may not be ransomed. He must certainly be put to death.
27.30: But every tithe from the land, whether from the seed of the land or from the fruit of the trees, belongs to the Lord. It is holy to the Lord.
27.31: If anyone redeems any of his tithe, he must add one-fifth to it.
27.32: The tithe from the herd or the flock, that is, every tenth animal that passes under the staff of the shepherd, shall be set apart as holy to the Lord.
27.33: The donor must not sort out the good from the bad, and he must not make any substitutions for it. If he makes a substitution for it, then both the first animal and its substitute shall be set apart as holy. It cannot be redeemed.
27.34: These are the commandments that the Lord commanded Moses for the people of Israel at Mount Sinai.

1.1: The Lord spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt. He said,
1.2: “Take a census of the entire community of the people of Israel, according to their clans and their fathers’ houses. Count the names of every male, one by one,
1.3: twenty years old and up, all who are of age to serve in Israel’s army. Aaron and you are to register them by their military units.
1.4: A man from each tribe will be with you. Every one of them will be the head of his fathers’ house.
1.5:
These are the names of the men who will assist you:
from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
1.6: from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
1.7: from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
1.8: from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
1.9: from Zebulun, Eliab the son of Helon;
1.11: from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
1.12: from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
1.13: from Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran;
1.14: from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
1.15: from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.”
1.16: These were the men chosen from the community, the chiefs of the tribes of their fathers. They were the heads of Israel’s divisions.
1.17: Moses and Aaron brought together these men, who had been designated by name.
1.18: They assembled the entire community on the first day of the second month, and they recorded the people’s ancestry by their clans, by their fathers’ houses, listing the names of those who were twenty years old and up, one by one.
1.19: Moses registered them in the Wilderness of Sinai, exactly as the Lord commanded him.
1.20: The male descendants of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn, were registered from their family records, according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, listing one by one the names of every male twenty years old and up, all who were of age to serve in the army.
1.21: Those who were registered from the tribe of Reuben totaled 46,500.
1.22: The male descendants of Simeon were registered from their family records, according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, listing one by one the names of every male twenty years old and up, all who were of age to serve in the army.
1.23: Those who were registered from the tribe of Simeon totaled 59,300.
1.24: The male descendants of Gad were registered from their family records, according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, listing the names of those twenty years old and up, all who were of age to serve in the army.
1.25: Those who were registered from the tribe of Gad totaled 45,650.
1.26: The male descendants of Judah were registered from their family records, according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, listing the names of those twenty years old and up, all who were of age to serve in the army.
1.27: Those who were registered from the tribe of Judah totaled 74,600.
1.28: The male descendants of Issachar were registered from their family records, according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, listing the names of those twenty years old and up, all who were of age to serve in the army.
1.29: Those who were registered from the tribe of Issachar totaled 54,400.
1.30: The male descendants of Zebulun were registered from their family records, according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, listing the names of those twenty years old and up, all who were of age to serve in the army.
1.31: Those who were registered from the tribe of Zebulun totaled 57,400.
1.32: The male descendants of Joseph who were the descendants of Ephraim were registered from their family records, according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, listing the names of those twenty years old and up, all who were of age to serve in the army.
1.33: Those who were registered from the tribe of Ephraim totaled 40,500.
1.34: Those who were male descendants of Manasseh were registered from their family records, according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, listing the names of those twenty years old and up, all who were of age to serve in the army.
1.35: Those who were registered from the tribe of Manasseh totaled 32,200.
1.36: The male descendants of Benjamin were registered from their family records, according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, listing the names of those twenty years old and up, all who were of age to serve in the army.
1.37: Those who were registered from the tribe of Benjamin totaled 35,400.
1.38: The male descendants of Dan were registered from their family records, according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, listing the names of those twenty years old and up, all who were of age to serve in the army.
1.39: Those who were registered from the tribe of Dan totaled 62,700.
1.40: The male descendants of Asher were registered from their family records, according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, listing the names of those twenty years old and up, all who were of age to serve in the army.
1.41: Those who were registered from the tribe of Asher totaled 41,500.
1.42: The male descendants of Naphtali were registered from their family records, according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, listing the names of those twenty years old and up, all who were of age to serve in the army.
1.43: Those who were registered from the tribe of Naphtali totaled 53,400.
1.44: These are the men who were registered by Moses and Aaron and twelve tribal chiefs of Israel, each representing his fathers’ house.
1.45: So all of the Israelite men twenty years old and up, who were of age to serve in Israel’s army, were registered according to their fathers’ houses.
1.47: But the Levites were not registered along with the others on the basis of their fathers’ tribe,
1.48: for the Lord had said to Moses,
1.49: “You are not to register the tribe of Levi, neither will you take a census of them along with the other Israelites.
1.50: Instead, appoint the Levites over the Dwelling of the Testimony and over all its furnishings and over everything that belongs to it. They are to carry the Dwelling and all its furnishings. They are to take care of it, and they are to camp around it.
1.51: Whenever the Dwelling is to move, the Levites will take it down, and whenever the Dwelling is to stop for a new camp, the Levites will set it up. Any unauthorized person who comes near it must be put to death.
1.52: The Israelites will set up camp, everyone in his own camp and under his own standard, according to their military divisions.
1.53: But the Levites will camp around the Dwelling of the Testimony so that wrath will not fall on the Israelite community. In this way the Levites will perform the duties for the Dwelling of the Testimony.”
1.54: So the Israelites did everything that the Lord commanded Moses, exactly as he commanded.

2.1: The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron as follows:
2.2: Each of the Israelites will camp under his own standard, with the banners for their fathers’ houses. They will camp around the Tent of Meeting at a distance from it.
2.3:
Those who camp on the east side toward the sunrise will be organized under the standard of Judah’s camp, according to their military units.
The tribal chief of Judah’s descendants is Nahshon son of Amminadab.
2.4: His unit, as registered, totals 74,600.
2.5: The tribe of Issachar will camp next to Judah. The tribal chief of Issachar’s descendants is Nethanel son of Zuar.
2.6: His unit, as registered, totals 54,400.
2.7: The tribe of Zebulun will be next. The tribal chief of Zebulun’s descendants is Eliab son of Helon.
2.8: His unit, as registered, totals 57,400.
2.9: All those registered in Judah’s camp are 186,400, according to their military units. They will set out first.
2.10:
Those who camp on the south side will be organized under the standard of Reuben’s camp, according to their military units.
The tribal chief of Reuben’s descendants is Elizur son of Shedeur.
2.11: His unit, as registered, totals 46,500.
2.12: The tribe of Simeon will camp next to Reuben. The tribal chief of Simeon’s descendants is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
2.13: His unit, as registered, totals 59,300.
2.14: The tribe of Gad will be next. The tribal chief of Gad’s descendants will be Eliasaph son of Deuel.
2.15: His unit, as registered, totals 45,650.
2.16: All those registered in Reuben’s camp are 151,450, according to their military units. They will set out second.
2.17: Then the Tent of Meeting will set out with the Levites’ camp, which is in the middle of the camps. They are to set out in the same order as they camp, each one in his place, following their standards.
2.18:
Those who camp on the west side will be organized under the standard of Ephraim’s camp, according to their military units.
The tribal chief of Ephraim’s descendants is Elishama son of Ammihud.
2.19: His unit, as registered, totals 40,500.
2.20: Next to Ephraim will be the tribe of Manasseh. The tribal chief of Manasseh’s descendants is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
2.21: His unit, as registered, totals 32,200.
2.22: The tribe of Benjamin will be next. The tribal chief of Benjamin’s descendants is Abidan son of Gideoni.
2.23: His unit, as registered, totals 35,400.
2.24: All those registered in Ephraim’s camp are 108,100, according to their military units. They will set out third.
2.25:
Those who camp on the north side will be organized under the standard of Dan’s camp, according to their military units.
The tribal chief of Dan’s descendants is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
2.26: His unit, as registered, totals 62,700.
2.27: Next to Dan will be the tribe of Asher. The tribal chief of Asher’s descendants will be Pagiel son of Ochran.
2.29: The tribe of Naphtali will be next. The tribal chief of Naphtali’s descendants is Ahira son of Enan.
2.31: All those registered in Dan’s camp are 157,600. They will set out last, following their standards.
2.32: These were the Israelites who were registered according to their fathers’ houses. All the men in the camps, organized according to their military units, as registered, totaled 603,550.
2.33: But the Levites were not registered among the Israelites, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
2.34: The Israelites did everything that the Lord commanded Moses. They camped around their standards, and they set out, every one of them by their clans, according to their fathers’ houses.

3.1: This is the family history of Aaron and Moses at the time when the Lord spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
3.2: These are the names of Aaron’s sons: Nadab the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
3.3: These are the names of Aaron’s sons, the anointed priests, whom he ordained to serve as priests.
3.4: Nadab and Abihu died in the presence of the Lord when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord in the Wilderness of Sinai, and they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the presence of Aaron their father.
3.5: The Lord spoke to Moses:
3.6: “Bring the tribe of Levi near and have them stand before Aaron the priest so that they may assist him.
3.7: They will perform the duties for him and for the entire congregation in front of the Tent of Meeting by doing the work for the Dwelling.
3.8: They will take care of all the furnishings for the Tent of Meeting and perform the duties of the Israelites by doing the work for the Dwelling.
3.9: You will give the Levites to Aaron and to his sons. They are completely given to him from among the Israelites.
3.10: But you will appoint Aaron and his sons, and they will serve in the priesthood. Any unauthorized person who goes near must be put to death.”
3.11: The Lord spoke to Moses,
3.12: “See, I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites instead of every firstborn that opens the womb among the Israelites. The Levites are mine,
3.13: for all the firstborn are mine. On the day that I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set apart for myself every firstborn in Israel, both human and animal. They are mine. I am the Lord.”
3.14: The Lord spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai,
3.15: “Register the Levites according to their fathers’ houses, by their clans. You are to register every male a month old and up.”
3.16: So Moses registered them as he was commanded by the word of the Lord.
3.17: These were the names of the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
3.18: These were the names of the sons of Gershon according to their clans: Libni and Shimei.
3.19: The sons of Kohath according to their clans were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
3.20:
The sons of Merari according to their clans were Mahli and Mushi.
The following were the clans of the Levites according to their fathers’ houses.
3.21: From Gershon came the Libnite clan and the Shimeite clan. These were the Gershonite clans.
3.22: Those who were registered, counting all the males who were a month old and up, were 7,500.
3.23: The Gershonite clans camped behind the Dwelling on the west side.
3.24: The tribal chief of the father’s house for the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.
3.25: The duties of the descendants of Gershon in the Tent of Meeting involved the dwelling and the tent, its coverings, and the screen for the entrance to the Tent of Meeting,
3.26: also the hangings of the courtyard, and the screen for the entrance to the courtyard which surrounds the Dwelling and the altar, and its ropes—everything related to this work.
3.27: From Kohath came the Amramite clan, the Izharite clan, the Hebronite clan, and the Uzzielite clan. These were the Kohathite clans.
3.28: Counting all the males who were a month old and up, there were 8,600 to perform the duties of the sanctuary.
3.29: The clans of the descendants of Kohath camped on the south side of the Dwelling.
3.30: The tribal chief of the father’s house for the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
3.31: Their duties involved the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the sanctuary utensils with which they serve, and the screen—everything related to this work.
3.32: The tribal chief over the Levite tribal chiefs was Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest. He was in charge of those performing the duties of the sanctuary.
3.33: From Merari came the Mahlite clan and the Mushite clan. These were the Merarite clans.
3.34: Those who were registered, counting all the males who were a month old and up, were 6,200.
3.35: The tribal chief of the father’s house for the Merarite clans was Zuriel son of Abihail. They camped on the north side of the Dwelling.
3.36: The appointed duties for the sons of Merari involved the Dwelling’s boards, its crossbars, its posts, its bases, all its equipment—everything related to this work,
3.37: also the posts for the surrounding courtyard, their bases, their tent pegs, and their ropes.
3.38: Those who camped in front of the Dwelling on the east side, in front of the Tent of Meeting, toward the sunrise, were Moses and Aaron and Aaron’s sons, who were performing the duties of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Any unauthorized person who goes near shall be put to death.
3.39: All of the Levities who were registered when the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron to register them according to their clans, every male a month old and up, were 22,000.
3.40: The Lord said to Moses, “Register all the firstborn males of the Israelites one month old and up, and make a list of their names.
3.41: You are to take the Levites for me—I am the Lord—instead of every firstborn among the Israelites, and take the livestock of the Levites instead of every firstborn among the livestock of the Israelites.”
3.42: So Moses registered all the firstborn among the Israelites as the Lord commanded.
3.43: All the firstborn males listed by name, one month old and up, when registered, totaled 22,273.
3.45: “Take the Levites instead of every firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites instead of their livestock. The Levites will be mine. I am the Lord.
3.46: For the redemption of the 273 firstborn Israelites who outnumber the Levites,
3.47: you are to collect five shekels apiece for each one, according to the sanctuary shekel (this shekel is twenty gerahs).
3.48: You are to give the money, the redemption price for the additional Israelites, to Aaron and his sons.”
3.49: Moses collected the redemption money from those who outnumbered the ones redeemed by the Levites who took their place.
3.50: He collected the money from the firstborn of the Israelites, 1,365 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
3.51: Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and to his sons, in obedience to the word of the Lord, just as the Lord commanded Moses.

4.1: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
4.2: to take a census of the descendants of Kohath among the Levites, by their clans, by their fathers’ houses,
4.3: from thirty years old to fifty years old, everyone eligible for the service of performing the tasks at the Tent of Meeting.
4.4: This is the work for the descendants of Kohath at the Tent of Meeting: to take care of the most holy things.
4.5: When the camp sets out, Aaron and his sons are to go into the Dwelling. They are to take down the veil that screens the ark, cover the Ark of the Testimony with it,
4.6: put a covering made from the hides of sea cows over it, spread a solid blue cloth over that, and insert its poles.
4.7: Over the table for the Bread of the Presence they are to spread a blue cloth and put the dishes, the small bowls, the larger bowls, and the pitchers for the drink offering on it. The bread that is continually there is to remain on it.
4.8: Then they are to spread a scarlet cloth over these things, cover them with a covering made from the hides of sea cows, and insert its poles.
4.9: They are to take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand used for light, its lamps, its snuffers, its fire pans, and all the jars of oil used to supply it.
4.10: They are to put the lampstand and all its accessories under a cover made from the hides of sea cows and put it on a carrying frame.
4.11: Over the golden altar they are to spread a blue cloth, cover it with a covering made from the hides of sea cows, and insert its poles.
4.12: They are to take all the utensils which they use in the sanctuary and put them in a blue cloth, cover them with a covering made from the hides of sea cows, and put them on a carrying frame.
4.13: They are to remove the fat-soaked ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.
4.14: They are to put on it all the utensils which they use around the altar: the fire pans, the meat hooks, the shovels, and the basins—the utensils of the altar. They will spread a covering made of the hides of sea cows over the altar and insert its poles.
4.15: After Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all the items of the sanctuary, when the camp sets out, the descendants of Kohath will come to carry them. But they are not to touch the sanctuary or they will die. The descendants of Kohath are to carry these things associated with the Tent of Meeting.
4.16: Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, shall be in charge of the lamp oil, the fragrant incense, the daily grain offering, and the anointing oil. He shall be in charge of the entire Dwelling, everything in it, the holy objects, and its furnishings.
4.17: The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron,
4.18: “Do not allow the tribe of the Kohathite clans to be cut off from among the Levites.
4.19: Do this for them so that they may live and not die when they come near the most holy things: Aaron and his sons are to go in and assign to each one of them what he is to do and what he is to carry.
4.20: But the Kohathites must not go in to see the sanctuary even for a moment or they will die.”
4.21: The Lord also told Moses
4.22: to take a census of the descendants of Gershon, according to their fathers’ houses, by their clans,
4.23: and to register those from thirty years old to fifty years old, everyone eligible for the service of doing the work at the Tent of Meeting.
4.24: This is the work for the Gershonite clans: the work of moving the Dwelling.
4.25: They are to carry the curtains of the Dwelling, the Tent of Meeting, its covering, and the covering made of sea cow hides that is on top of that, the screen for the entrance to the Tent of Meeting,
4.26: the hangings for the courtyard, the screen for the entrance through the gate into the courtyard which surrounds the Dwelling and the altar, the ropes, and all the items related to this work. They are responsible for everything that is to be done with these things.
4.27: All the work of the descendants of the Gershonites, everything they are to carry and all the work they are to do, is to be done at the command of Aaron and his sons. You are to assign to each of them everything they are to carry.
4.28: This is the work for the clans of the descendants of the Gershonites in regard to the Tent of Meeting. They are to serve under the direction of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
4.29: As for the descendants of Merari, register them according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses.
4.30: Register all of them who are between thirty years old and fifty years old, everyone eligible for service, to do the work for the Tent of Meeting.
4.31: This is what they are responsible for as their entire work at the Tent of Meeting: to carry the Dwelling’s boards, its crossbars, its posts, its bases,
4.32: the posts of the surrounding courtyard and their bases, their tent pegs, their ropes with all their equipment, and everything related to this work. You are to specify by name the items that they are responsible to carry.
4.33: This is the work for the clans of the descendants of Merari, regarding all their work in regard to the Tent of Meeting, under the direction of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
4.34: Moses, Aaron, and the tribal chiefs of the community registered the descendants of the Kohathites according to their clans and their fathers’ houses,
4.35: from thirty years old to fifty years old, everyone eligible for service, for work at the Tent of Meeting.
4.36: The ones registered according to their clans were 2,750.
4.37: These were the ones registered from the clans of the Kohathites, all those who worked at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron registered them according to the Lord’s command through Moses.
4.38: The descendants of Gershon were registered according to their clans and according to their fathers’ houses,
4.39: from thirty years old to fifty years old, everyone eligible for service, for work at the Tent of Meeting.
4.40: The ones registered according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses, were 2,630.
4.41: These were the ones registered from the clans of the descendants of Gershon, all those who worked at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron registered them according to the Lord’s command.
4.42: The clans of the descendants of Merari were registered according to their clans, according to their fathers’ houses,
4.43: from thirty years old to fifty years old, everyone eligible for service, for work at the Tent of Meeting.
4.44: Those registered by their clans were 3,200.
4.45: These were the ones registered from the clans of the descendants of Merari. Moses and Aaron registered them according to the Lord’s command through Moses.
4.46: Every one of the Levites was registered. Moses and Aaron and the tribal chiefs of Israel registered them according to their clans and their fathers’ houses,
4.47: from thirty years old to fifty years old, everyone who was eligible to perform the work of serving at or carrying the Tent of Meeting.
4.49: According to the Lord’s command, they were registered by Moses, along with what each man was assigned to do and to carry. They were registered just as the Lord commanded Moses.

5.1: The Lord spoke to Moses:
5.2: “Command the Israelites to send outside of the camp everyone who has an impure skin disease, everyone who has a bodily discharge, and everyone who is unclean because of contact with a dead body.
5.3: You must send them away, male or female. You must send them outside of the camp so that they will not defile their camps, where I dwell in their midst.”
5.4: The Israelites did exactly that and sent them outside of the camp. The Israelites did just as the Lord said to Moses.
5.5: The Lord spoke to Moses and told him
5.6:
to tell the Israelites this:
Whenever a man or a woman commits any wrong against another person and so in this way is unfaithful to the Lord, that person must be held responsible.
5.7: Such people are to confess the wrong which they have done. They are to make full restitution for their guilt, then add one fifth of its value on top of that and give it to the person they have wronged.
5.8: But if the wronged person has no next-of-kin to receive the restitution, the restitution goes to the Lord for the priest, in addition to the atonement ram, with which the priest will make atonement for him.
5.9: Every elevated offering that the Israelites present to the priest will belong to the priest.
5.10: Anyone’s holy things are his own, but whatever anyone gives to the priest is the priest’s.
5.11: The Lord told Moses to speak to the Israelites and tell them this:
5.12: If any man’s wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him,
5.13: and another man lies down with her, but this remains hidden from her husband and she is not found out, she has defiled herself even though there is no witness against her and she was not caught in the act.
5.14: If a feeling of jealousy comes over her husband and he becomes jealous of his wife who has defiled herself, or if a feeling of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife, even though she has not defiled herself,
5.15: then the man is to bring his wife to the priest. He is also to bring an offering on her behalf: two quarts of barley flour. He is not to pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, a grain offering for remembrance, to reveal guilt.
5.16: The priest is to bring her near and present her before the Lord.
5.17: The priest is to take holy water in a clay vessel, take some of the dust that is on the floor of the Dwelling, and put it into the water.
5.18: The priest is to present the woman before the Lord, let down the woman’s hair, and put into her hands the grain offering for remembrance, which is the grain offering for jealousy. The priest is to have in his hands the bitter water that brings a curse.
5.19: The priest will make her take an oath, and he will tell the woman, “If no man has slept with you, and if you have not gone astray by becoming defiled while married to your husband, may this bitter water that brings a curse not affect you.
5.20: But if you have gone astray while married to your husband, and if you are defiled and another man besides your husband has had sex with you—”
5.21: Then the priest will make the woman take an oath with a curse, and the priest will tell the woman, “May the Lord make you an object of cursing and swearing among your people when the Lord allows your thigh to shrivel and your belly to swell.
5.22: May this water that brings a curse go inside you and make your belly swell and your thigh shrivel.” The woman will say, “Amen, Amen.”
5.23: The priest is to write these curses on a scroll and wipe them off into the bitter water.
5.24: He will make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse. The water that brings a curse will enter into her and become bitter.
5.25: The priest will take the grain offering for jealousy out of the woman’s hand, wave the grain offering before the Lord, and bring it to the altar.
5.26: The priest will take a handful of the grain offering as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar. Afterward he will make the woman drink the water.
5.27: When he has made her drink the water, if she has defiled herself and has been unfaithful to her husband, the water that brings a curse will enter into her and become bitter. Her belly will swell, and her thigh will shrivel. The woman will be an object of cursing among her people.
5.28: If the woman has not defiled herself but is clean, then she will be unaffected and will be able to conceive children.
5.29: This is the law regarding jealousy when a wife, while married to her husband, goes astray and defiles herself,
5.30: or when a feeling of jealousy comes over a husband and he is jealous of his wife. Then the man will present the woman before the Lord, and the priest will apply this entire procedure to her.
5.31: The man will be free from guilt, but that woman will bear her guilt.

6.1: The Lord told Moses to speak to the Israelites and tell them these things:
6.2: When a man or woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate oneself to the Lord,
6.3: he is to abstain from wine and beer. He may not drink vinegar made from wine or beer. He may not drink any grape juice. He may not eat fresh grapes or raisins.
6.4: During his entire separation, he is not to eat anything at all that comes from the grapevine, from the seeds to the skins.
6.5: During his entire vow of separation no razor is to pass over his head, until the time that he has separated himself to the Lord has been completed. He will be set apart as holy. He is to let the hair of his head grow long.
6.6: During the entire time that he separates himself to the Lord he may not go near a dead body.
6.7: He may not defile himself even for his father or his mother or for his brother or his sister when they die, because his sign of separation for God is on his head.
6.8: During the entire time of his separation he is set apart as holy to the Lord.
6.9: If someone near him dies suddenly, thereby defiling the head of hair that marks his separation, he is to shave his head on the day when he is purified. On the seventh day he is to shave it.
6.10: On the eighth day he will bring two turtledoves or two pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
6.11: The priest will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. He will make atonement for him, because he sinned on account of the dead body. On that same day, he is to consecrate his head.
6.12: He will establish a new time of separation to the Lord. He will bring a year-old male lamb as a restitution offering. His previous time of separation will not count, because his separation was defiled.
6.13: This is the law for the Nazirite when the time of his separation is over: He is to be brought to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
6.14: He will bring this as his offering to the Lord: a year-old male lamb without defect as a whole burnt offering, a year-old female lamb without defect as a sin offering, one ram without defect as a fellowship offering,
6.15: a basket of unleavened round loaves made with fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened wafers coated with oil, along with the specified grain offerings and drink offerings.
6.16: The priest will bring them before the Lord and will offer the Nazirite’s sin offering and burnt offering.
6.17: The priest will offer the ram as the sacrifice for the fellowship offering to the Lord, along with the basket of unleavened bread. The priest will also offer the specified grain offering and drink offering.
6.18: The Nazirite is to shave the hair on his head, that marks his separation at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. He is to take the hair from his head, that marks his separation, and put it on the fire which is under the sacrifice for the fellowship offering.
6.19: The priest will take the boiled shoulder from the ram and one unleavened round loaf out of the basket and one unleavened wafer, and put them into the palms of the Nazirite after he has shaved the head that marks his separation.
6.20: The priest will wave them as a wave offering before the Lord. This is the holy portion for the priest, together with the breast that is waved and the thigh that is elevated. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.
6.21: This is the law for the Nazirite who vows his offering to the Lord according to his separation, in addition to whatever else he can afford. Just as he has made this vow, so he must carry it out according to the law governing his separation.
6.22: The Lord told Moses
6.23: to speak to Aaron and to his sons and to tell them to bless the Israelites with these words:
6.24: The Lord bless you and keep you.
6.25:
The Lord make his face shine on you
and be gracious to you.
6.26:
The Lord look on you with favor
and give you peace.
6.27: In this way they will put my name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.

7.1: On the day that Moses finished setting up the Dwelling, he anointed and consecrated it with all of its furnishings and the altar with all of its utensils. He anointed and consecrated them.
7.2: The tribal chiefs of Israel, the heads of their fathers’ houses, brought offerings. These were the chiefs of the tribes, who were in charge of the registration.
7.3: They brought as their offering before the Lord six covered carts and twelve oxen—a cart for every two tribal chiefs and an ox for every tribal chief. They presented them in front of the Dwelling.
7.4: The Lord spoke to Moses:
7.5: “Accept these gifts from them so that they may be used for doing the work at the Tent of Meeting. You are to give them to the Levites as each one’s work requires.”
7.6: Moses took the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
7.7: He gave two carts and four oxen to the descendants of Gershon as their work required.
7.8: He gave four carts and eight oxen to the descendants of Merari, as required for their work under the direction of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
7.9: But to the descendants of Kohath he did not give any, because their work was to carry the holy things on their own shoulders.
7.10: The tribal chiefs also brought offerings for the dedication of the altar on the day that it was anointed. The tribal chiefs brought their offerings before the altar.
7.11: The Lord said to Moses, “Each day one tribal chief will bring his offering for the dedication of the altar.”
7.12: On the first day, the one who brought his offering was Nahshon son of Amminadab from the tribe of Judah.
7.13: His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels, one silver sprinkling basin weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
7.14: one small gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
7.15: one young bull, one ram, one year-old male lamb for a whole burnt offering;
7.16: one male goat for a sin offering;
7.17: and for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering: two head of cattle, five rams, five male breeding goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
7.18: On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, the tribal chief of Issachar, brought his offering.
7.19: He brought for his offering: one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels, one silver sprinkling basin weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
7.20: one small gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
7.21: one young bull, one ram, one year-old male lamb for a whole burnt offering;
7.22: one male goat for a sin offering;
7.23: and for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering: two head of cattle, five rams, five male breeding goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
7.24: On the third day it was the tribal chief of Zebulun’s descendants, Eliab son of Helon.
7.25: His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels, one silver sprinkling basin weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
7.26: one small gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
7.27: one young bull, one ram, one year-old male lamb for a whole burnt offering;
7.28: one male goat for a sin offering;
7.29: and for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering: two head of cattle, five rams, five male breeding goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.
7.30: On the fourth day it was the tribal chief of Reuben’s descendants, Elizur son of Shedeur.
7.31: His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels, one silver sprinkling basin weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
7.32: one small gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
7.33: one young bull, one ram, one year-old male lamb for a whole burnt offering;
7.34: one male goat for a sin offering;
7.35: and for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering: two head of cattle, five rams, five male breeding goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.
7.36: On the fifth day it was the tribal chief of Simeon’s descendants, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
7.37: His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels, one silver sprinkling basin weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
7.38: one small gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
7.39: one young bull, one ram, one year-old male lamb for a whole burnt offering;
7.40: one male goat for a sin offering;
7.41: and for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering: two head of cattle, five rams, five male breeding goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
7.42: On the sixth day it was the tribal chief of Gad’s descendants, Eliasaph son of Deuel.
7.43: His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels, one silver sprinkling basin weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
7.44: one small gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
7.45: one young bull, one ram, one year-old male lamb for a whole burnt offering;
7.46: one male goat for a sin offering;
7.47: and for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering: two head of cattle, five rams, five male breeding goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.
7.48: On the seventh day it was the tribal chief of Ephraim’s descendants, Elishama son of Ammihud.
7.49: His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels, one silver sprinkling basin weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
7.50: one small gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
7.51: one young bull, one ram, one year-old male lamb for a whole burnt offering;
7.52: one male goat for a sin offering;
7.53: and for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering: two head of cattle, five rams, five male breeding goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.
7.54: On the eighth day it was the tribal chief of Manasseh’s descendants, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
7.55: His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels, one silver sprinkling basin weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
7.56: one small gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
7.57: one young bull, one ram, one year-old male lamb for a whole burnt offering;
7.58: one male goat for a sin offering;
7.59: and for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering: two head of cattle, five rams, five male breeding goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
7.60: On the ninth day it was the tribal chief of Benjamin’s descendants, Abidan son of Gideoni.
7.61: His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels, one silver sprinkling basin weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
7.62: one small gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
7.63: one young bull, one ram, one year-old male lamb for a whole burnt offering;
7.64: one male goat for a sin offering;
7.65: and for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering: two head of cattle, five rams, five male breeding goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Abidan son of Gideoni.
7.66: On the tenth day it was the tribal chief of Dan’s descendants, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
7.67: His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels, one silver sprinkling basin weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
7.68: one small gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
7.69: one young bull, one ram, one year-old male lamb for a whole burnt offering;
7.70: one male goat for a sin offering;
7.71: and for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering: two head of cattle, five rams, five male breeding goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
7.72: On the eleventh day it was the tribal chief of Asher’s descendants, Pagiel son of Ochran.
7.73: His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels, one silver sprinkling basin weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
7.74: one small gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
7.75: one young bull, one ram, one year-old male lamb for a whole burnt offering;
7.76: one male goat for a sin offering;
7.77: and for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering: two head of cattle, five rams, five male breeding goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ochran.
7.78: On the twelfth day it was the tribal chief of Naphtali’s descendants, Ahira son of Enan.
7.79: His offering was one silver dish weighing one hundred thirty shekels, one silver sprinkling basin weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
7.80: one small gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
7.81: one young bull, one ram, one year-old male lamb for a whole burnt offering;
7.82: one male goat for a sin offering;
7.83: and for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering: two head of cattle, five rams, five male breeding goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.
7.84: These were the offerings from the tribal chiefs of Israel for the dedication of the altar on the day that it was anointed: twelve silver dishes, twelve silver sprinkling basins, twelve small gold bowls.
7.85: Each silver dish weighed one hundred thirty shekels, and each sprinkling basin weighed seventy shekels. All the silver vessels weighed two thousand four hundred shekels according to the sanctuary shekel.
7.86: The twelve gold bowls, filled with incense, weighed ten shekels each, according to the sanctuary shekel. All the gold bowls weighed one hundred twenty shekels.
7.87: All the cattle for the whole burnt offering were twelve young bulls, twelve rams, twelve one-year-old male lambs, along with their grain offerings. Also there were twelve male breeding goats for a sin offering.
7.88: All the cattle for the sacrifice of the fellowship offering were twenty-four young bulls, sixty rams, sixty male breeding goats, and sixty one-year-old male lambs. These were the offerings for the dedication of the altar after it was anointed.
7.89: When Moses went into the Tent of Meeting to speak with the Lord, he heard the Lord’s voice speaking to him from between the two cherubim above the atonement seat that was on the Ark of the Covenant. In this way the Lord spoke to him.

8.1: The Lord spoke to Moses:
8.2: “Speak to Aaron and tell him, ‘When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps are to give light in front of the lampstand.’”
8.3: So that is what Aaron did. He set up the lamps to light the area in front of the lampstand, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
8.4: This was how the lampstand was made: It was a work of hammered gold. From its base to its blossoms, it was one hammered piece. So the lampstand was made according to the pattern that the Lord had shown Moses.
8.5: The Lord told Moses
8.6: to take the Levites from among the Israelites and to do the following to make them ceremonially clean:
8.7: This is what you are to do to them to make them ceremonially clean: Sprinkle the water of purification on them. Have them shave their entire body with a razor, wash their clothes, and purify themselves.
8.8: Then they are to take a young bull from the herd with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil. You are to take another young bull from the herd for a sin offering.
8.9: You are to present the Levites in front of the Tent of Meeting. You are to assemble the entire Israelite community.
8.10: You are to present the Levites before the Lord. The Israelites will place their hands on the Levites.
8.11: Then Aaron will offer the Levites before the Lord as a wave offering on behalf of the Israelites. They are to do the work of the Lord.
8.12: The Levites are to place their hands on the heads of the young bulls. You then will offer the one young bull as a sin offering and the other young bull as a whole burnt offering to the Lord to make atonement for the Levites.
8.13: You will have the Levites stand in front of Aaron and his sons, and you will offer them as a wave offering to the Lord.
8.14: In this way you are to set apart the Levites from the other Israelites, and the Levites will be mine.
8.15: After you have purified them and offered them as a wave offering, the Levites will go to work at the Tent of Meeting,
8.16: because only they are given to me as servants from among the Israelites. In place of every firstborn from the womb, the firstborn of every Israelite, I have taken the Levites for myself.
8.17: For all the firstborn among the Israelites are mine, both human and animal. On the day that I struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set the firstborn of the Israelites apart for myself.
8.18: But I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites.
8.19: From among the Israelites I have given only the Levites to Aaron and his sons to do the work of the people of Israel at the Tent of Meeting and to make atonement for the people of Israel so that there will not be any plague among the Israelites when the Israelites approach the sanctuary.
8.20: Moses, Aaron, and the entire community of the people of Israel did for the Levites just as they had been told. The Israelites did for them everything that the Lord commanded Moses in regard to the Levites.
8.21: The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothing. Aaron offered them as a wave offering before the Lord and made atonement for them to purify them.
8.22: After that, the Levites went to do their work at the Tent of Meeting in the presence of Aaron and his sons. Just as the Lord had commanded Moses about the Levites, that is exactly what they did for them.
8.24: “This applies to the Levites: From twenty-five years of age and up, they are to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
8.25: But when they are fifty years old, they are to retire from the service and no longer work.
8.26: They may assist their brothers at the Tent of Meeting in performing their duties, but they are not to do the work. This is exactly what you are to do in regard to the Levites and their duties.”

9.1: The Lord spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai, during the first month of the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt. He said,
9.2: “The people of Israel are to observe the Passover at its appointed time.
9.3: On the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight, you will observe it at its appointed time. You will observe it according to all its regulations and all its ordinances.”
9.4: Moses told the Israelites to observe the Passover.
9.5: They observed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, at twilight, in the Wilderness of Sinai. The Israelites did everything just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
9.6: There were some men, however, who were unclean because of contact with a dead body. So they were not able to observe the Passover on that day. They went before Moses and Aaron on that same day.
9.7: These men said to him, “We are unclean because of a dead body. Why should we be kept from presenting the offering of the Lord at its appointed time among the people of Israel?”
9.8: So Moses said to them, “Wait and let me hear what the Lord commands concerning you.”
9.9: The Lord spoke to Moses
9.10:
and told him to tell the Israelites this:
If any one of you or your descendants is unclean because of contact with a dead body or is on a distant journey, he may still observe the Passover to the Lord.
9.11: Such people are to observe it during the second month, on the fourteenth day, at twilight. They are to eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
9.12: They must not leave any of it until morning. They are not to break a single one of its bones. They are to observe the Passover according to every regulation for it.
9.13: But anyone who is clean and is not on a journey yet fails to observe the Passover will be cut off from his people. He will bear his sin because he did not present the offering of the Lord at its appointed time.
