11.31: But if we judged ourselves, we would not be undergoing judgment.
11.32: However, when we undergo judgment, we are being disciplined by the Lord so that we may not be condemned with the world.
11.33: Therefore, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
11.34: If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home so that your coming together may not result in judgment. The rest of my instructions I will give when I come.

12.1: Now concerning spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed.
12.2: You know that when you were pagans, you were deceived and somehow led away to mute idols.
12.3: Therefore I am informing you that no one speaking by God’s Spirit says, “A curse be upon Jesus,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.
12.4: There are various kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.
12.5: There are different kinds of ministries, and yet the same Lord.
12.6: There are various kinds of activity, but the same God, who produces all of them in everyone.
12.7: Each person is given a manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.
12.8: To one person a message of wisdom is given by the Spirit; to another, a message of knowledge, as the same Spirit provides it;
12.9: by the same Spirit, faith is given to someone else; and to another, the same Spirit gives healing gifts.
12.10: Another is given powers to do miracles; another, the gift of prophecy; another, the evaluating of spirits; someone else, different kinds of tongues; and another, the interpretation of tongues.
12.11: One and the same Spirit produces all of these, distributing them to each one individually as he desires.
12.12: For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so also is Christ.
12.13: For by one Spirit we all were baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free people, and we were all caused to drink one Spirit.
12.14: Furthermore, the body is not one member, but many.
12.15: If the foot says, “Because I am not a hand, I am not part of the body,” it does not on that account cease to be part of the body.
12.16: If the ear says, “Because I am not an eye, I am not part of the body,” it does not on that account cease to be part of the body.
12.17: If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?
12.18: But now God has arranged the members in the body, each and every one of them, as he desired.
12.19: If they were all one member, where would the body be?
12.20: But as it is, there are many members, yet one body.
12.21: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”
12.22: On the contrary, the members of the body that seem to be weaker are much more necessary.
12.23: As for the parts of the body we consider less honorable, these we provide with more honor. We treat our unpresentable parts with more modesty,
12.24: whereas our presentable parts have no such need. But God put the body together in a way that gave more honor to the parts that lack it.
12.25: He did it so that there might not be any division in the body, but that the members might all have the same concern for one another.
12.26: So if one member suffers, all the members suffer with it, or if one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
12.27: You are the body of Christ, and individually you are members of it.
12.28: And God appointed in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers; then miracles, healing gifts, helpful acts, leadership abilities, kinds of tongues.
12.29: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all miracle workers?
12.30: Do all have healing gifts? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
12.31: But eagerly seek the greater gifts. And now, I am going to show you a more excellent way.

13.1: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels but do not have love, I have become a noisy gong or a clanging cymbal.
13.2: If I have the gift of prophecy and know all the mysteries and have all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.
13.3: If I give away everything I own, and if I give up my body that I may be burned but do not have love, I gain nothing.
13.4: Love is patient. Love is kind. Love does not envy. It does not brag. It is not arrogant.
13.5: It does not behave indecently. It is not selfish. It is not irritable. It does not keep a record of wrongs.
13.6: It does not rejoice over unrighteousness but rejoices with the truth.
13.7: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
13.8: Love never comes to an end. But if there are prophetic gifts, they will be done away with; if tongues, they will cease; if knowledge, it will be done away with.
13.9: For we know only in part, and we prophesy only in part,
13.10: but when that which is complete has come, that which is partial will be done away with.
13.11: When I was a child, I spoke like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I put away childish things.
13.12: Now we see indirectly using a mirror, but then we will see face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know fully, just as I was fully known.
13.13: So now these three remain: faith, hope, and love—and the greatest of these is love.

14.1: Keep on pursuing love, and eagerly seek spiritual gifts, but especially prophecy.
14.2: For the person who speaks in a tongue speaks to God, not to people. For no one understands him, but he speaks mysteries in the Spirit.
14.3: However, the person who prophesies speaks to people things that edify, encourage, and comfort.
14.4: The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the church.
14.5: I would like all of you to speak in tongues, but I would prefer that you prophesy. For the person who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets so that the church may be built up.
14.6: Brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what good will I do you, unless I communicate to you a revelation, or some knowledge, or a prophecy, or some teaching?
14.7: Even lifeless instruments that produce sound, such as a flute or a harp, if they do not make the notes distinct from one another, how will anyone know what is being played on the flute or harp?
14.8: If the trumpet makes an uncertain sound, who will get ready for battle?
14.9: So also with you: Unless you use your tongue to produce intelligible speech, how will anyone know what is being spoken? To be sure, you will be speaking only into the air.
14.10: There are perhaps ever so many kinds of languages in the world, and not one of them is without meaning.
14.11: Accordingly, if I do not understand the language, I will be a foreigner to the speaker, and he will be a foreigner to me.
14.12: So also with you: Since you are eager for spiritual gifts, seek to use them abundantly in a way that will build up the church.
14.13: That is why a person who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.
14.14: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my understanding is unfruitful.
14.15: So what is to be done? I will pray using my spirit, and I will pray also using my understanding. I will sing using my spirit, and I will sing also using my understanding.
14.16: Otherwise, how will an uninformed person say the “Amen” after you give thanks, since he does not know what you are saying?
14.17: To be sure, you are giving thanks well enough, but the other person is not being built up.
14.18: I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
14.19: But in the church I would rather speak five words with my understanding, in order to instruct others, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
14.20: Brothers, do not be children in your thinking, but be like babies in regard to evil, and be mature in your thinking.
14.21: It is written in the law, “By different tongues and by foreign lips I will speak to this people, and even so, they will not listen to me, says the Lord.”
14.22: Therefore, tongues are a sign meant for unbelievers, not believers, whereas prophecy is for believers, not unbelievers.
14.23: So if the whole church comes together in the same place and all speak in tongues, and uninformed visitors or unbelievers come in, won’t they say that you are crazy?
14.24: But if all prophesy and some unbeliever or uninformed visitor comes in, he is reproved by all and judged by all,
14.25: the secrets of his heart are revealed, and under those circumstances he will fall down on his face and worship God, declaring, “God really is among you!”
14.26: So, brothers, what is to be done? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, or a teaching, or a revelation, or an utterance in a tongue, or an interpretation. Let all things be done in a way that builds people up.
14.27: If someone speaks in a tongue, limit it to two or at most three (speaking one at a time), and have one person interpret.
14.28: But if there is no interpreter, he is to keep silent in the church and keep his speaking between himself and God.
14.29: Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others carefully evaluate what was said.
14.30: But if a revelation comes to another person as he sits there, let the first person become silent.
14.31: For you all can do your prophesying one at a time, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged.
14.32: The spirits of the prophets are also subject to the prophets,
14.33:
for God is not a God of disorder, but of peace.
As in all the churches of the saints,
14.34: the women are to keep silent in the churches, for they are not permitted to speak. Instead they are to be subordinate, as also the Law says.
14.35: If they desire to learn something, let them ask their own men at home, because it is shameful for a woman to speak in the church.
14.36: Or are you the ones from whom the word of God has gone out? Or did it come to you alone?
14.37: If anyone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual person, let him recognize that the things I write to you are the Lord’s commands.
14.38: But if anyone disregards them, he should be disregarded.
14.39: So, brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
14.40: But let all things be done decently and in good order.

15.1: Brothers, I am going to call your attention to the gospel that I preached to you. You received it, and you took your stand on it.
15.2: You are also being saved by that gospel that was expressed in the words I preached to you, if you keep your hold on it—unless you believed in vain.
15.3:
For I delivered to you as of first importance what I also received:
that Christ died for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures,
15.4:
that he was buried,
that he was raised on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures,
15.5: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve.
15.6: After that he appeared to over five hundred brothers at the same time, most of whom are still alive, but some have fallen asleep.
15.7: Then he appeared to James, and then to all the apostles.
15.8: Last of all, he appeared also to me, the stillborn child, so to speak.
15.9: For I am the least of the apostles, and I am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted God’s church.
15.10: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me was not ineffective. On the contrary, I worked more than all of them (and yet it wasn’t my doing, but it was the grace of God, which was with me, that did it).
15.11: So whether it is I or they, that is what we preach, and that is what you believed.
15.12: Now if it is preached that Christ has been raised from the dead, how is it that some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
15.13: If there is no resurrection of the dead, not even Christ has been raised.
15.14: And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is pointless, and your faith is pointless too.
15.15: Then we are even guilty of giving false testimony about God, because we testified about God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise, if it were true that the dead are not raised.
15.16: For if the dead are not raised, not even Christ has been raised.
15.17: And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.
15.18: Then it also follows that those who fell asleep in Christ perished.
15.19: If our hope in Christ applies only to this life, we are the most pitiful people of all.
15.20: But in fact Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
15.21: For since death came by a man, the resurrection of the dead also is going to come by a man.
15.22: For as in Adam they all die, so also in Christ they all will be made alive.
15.23: But each in his own order: Christ as the firstfruits and then Christ’s people, at his coming.
15.24: Then comes the end, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, after he has done away with every other ruler and every other authority and power.
15.25: For he must reign “until he has put all his enemies under his feet.”
15.26: Death is the last enemy to be done away with.
15.27: Certainly, “he has put all things in subjection under his feet.” Now when it says that all things have been put in subjection, obviously that does not include the one who subjected all things to him.
15.28: But when all things have been subjected to him, then the Son himself will also be subjected to the one who subjected all things to him, in order that God may be all in all.
15.29: Otherwise, what will those people do who get baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why do they even get baptized for them?
15.30: Why do we live in danger every hour?
15.31: Day by day I face death, as surely as I boast about you, brothers, in Christ Jesus our Lord.
15.32: If I fought wild animals in Ephesus with human motives, what good did it do me? If the dead are not raised, then “let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
15.33: Do not be deceived! “Keeping bad company corrupts good morals.”
15.34: Use sober judgment, as is right, and do not sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
15.35: But someone will object, “How can it be that the dead are raised? With what kind of body are they going to come?”
15.36: You are being foolish. What you sow is not made alive unless it dies.
15.37: And what you sow is not the body that will be, but a bare seed, perhaps of wheat or some other grain.
15.38: But God gives it a body of the kind he wanted it to have, and to each of the seeds he gives its own body.
15.39: Flesh is not all the same kind. Instead, people have one kind of flesh, animals have another kind, birds another, and fish yet another.
15.40: There are also celestial bodies and bodies on earth, but the glory of the celestial bodies differs from that of the bodies on earth.
15.41: There is one glory of the sun, another of the moon, and another of the stars; in fact, one star differs from another in glory.
15.42: That is the way the resurrection of the dead will be. What is sown is perishable; it is raised imperishable.
15.43: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
15.44:
It is sown as a natural body; it is raised as a spiritual body.
If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
15.45: So also it is written, “The first man, Adam, became a living natural being.” The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
15.46: However, that which is spiritual is not first; rather, first comes the natural, then the spiritual.
15.47: The first man is of the earth, made of dust. The second man is the Lord from heaven.
15.48: As was the man made of dust, so are the people who are made of dust, and as is the heavenly man, so the heavenly people will be.
15.49: And just as we have borne the image of the man made of dust, let us also bear the image of the heavenly man.
15.50: Now I say this, brothers: Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, and what is perishable is not going to inherit what is imperishable.
15.51: Look, I tell you a mystery. We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,
15.52: in a moment, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
15.53: For this perishable body must put on imperishability, and this mortal body must put on immortality.
15.54:
But once this perishable body has put on imperishability, and this mortal body has put on immortality, then what is written will be fulfilled:
Death is swallowed up in victory.
15.55:
Death, where is your sting?
Grave, where is your victory?
15.56: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
15.57: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
15.58: Therefore, my dear brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.

16.1: Now concerning the collection for the saints, do as I directed the churches in Galatia to do.
16.2: On the first day of every week, each of you is to set something aside in keeping with whatever he gains, saving it up at home, so that when I come, no collections will need to be carried out.
16.3: When I arrive, those whom you approve will be provided with letters, and I will send these representatives to deliver your gracious gift to Jerusalem.
16.4: If it is appropriate for me to go also, they will go with me.
16.5: I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I am going to go through Macedonia.
16.6: Perhaps I will have an extended stay with you or even spend the winter, so that you may send me on my way, wherever I go.
16.7: For I do not wish to see you now in passing. I hope to stay with you for a while, if the Lord permits.
16.8: But I will stay on in Ephesus until Pentecost,
16.9: because a door has opened for me, a great opportunity for action, and there are many adversaries.
16.10: But if Timothy comes, make sure he has no reason to be afraid while he is with you, for he does the work of the Lord, as I do.
16.11: Therefore let no one despise him. But send him on his way in peace so that he may come to me, because I am expecting him, and so are the brothers with me.
16.12: Now concerning our brother Apollos, I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers. It was not at all his desire to go now, but he will when he has an opportunity.
16.13: Keep alert. Stand firm in the faith. Demonstrate manly courage. Be strong.
16.14: Let everything you do be done in love.
16.15: Brothers, you know Stephanas and his household. You know that they are the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they volunteered for service to the saints.
16.16: I urge that you also submit to them and to everyone who joins in and works hard.
16.17: I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus came, because they supplied what was lacking on your part,
16.18: and they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge such people.
16.19: The churches in the province of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, together with the church that meets in their house.
16.20: All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
16.21: This greeting is written by me, Paul, with my own hand.
16.22: If anyone does not love the Lord—let him be under a curse! Marana tha!
16.23: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
16.24: My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

1.1:
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother,
To the church of God that is in Corinth, together with all the saints who are everywhere in Achaia:
1.2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort,
1.4: who comforts us in all our trouble, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the same comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
1.5: For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so through Christ our comfort also overflows.
1.6: If we are troubled, it is for your comfort and salvation. If we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which produces in you the ability to endure the same sufferings that we are also suffering.
1.7: Our hope for you is sure, since we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so you also share in our comfort.
1.8: Brothers, we do not want you to be unaware of the trouble that happened to us in the province of Asia. We were burdened so greatly, so far beyond our ability to bear it, that we even gave up hope of living.
1.9: Yes, we even felt the sentence of death within ourselves. This happened so that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead.
1.10: He rescued us from such a terrible death, and he will continue to rescue us. We have set our hope on him that he will also rescue us again,
1.11: as you join in helping us with your prayers for us. Then many people will thank God for the gracious gift given to us through many prayers.
1.12: Indeed, this is our boast: Our conscience testifies that we have conducted ourselves in the world with God-given holiness and sincerity, not with the wisdom of the flesh, but rather in God’s grace—especially toward you.
1.13: In fact, we are not writing you anything other than what you read or also understand. And I hope you will understand completely—
1.14: as you have also understood us in part—that on the day of our Lord Jesus we are going to be your reason for boasting, just as you are our reason.
1.15: In this confidence, I was planning to visit you first, so that you would have a second gracious gift.
1.16: Then I planned to travel from you on to Macedonia, and to return again from Macedonia to you to receive help from you on my way to Judea.
1.17: So when I made this plan, I did not do it lightly, did I? Or the things I plan, am I planning them the way the sinful flesh does, so that I would be saying both “Yes, yes” and “No, no” at the same time?
1.18: As surely as God is faithful, our message to you is not “Yes” and “No.”
1.19: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us (by me, Silas, and Timothy), was not “Yes” and “No,” but in him the “Yes” stands firm.
1.20: In fact, as many promises as God has made, they have always been “Yes” in him. For that reason we also say “Amen” through him to the glory of God.
1.21: God is the one who makes both us and you to be strong in Christ. He anointed us.
1.22: He sealed us as his own and gave us the Spirit as the down payment in our hearts.
1.23: I call God as my witness, on my very life, that I avoided coming to Corinth in order to spare you.
1.24: Not that we are lording it over your faith, but we are working together with you for your joy. For you stand firm by faith.

2.1: That is why I made up my mind that I would not make another sad visit to you.
2.2: For if I make you sad, then who is there to make me glad, other than those I made sad?
2.3: I am writing for this very purpose: That when I arrive, I will not be made sad by those who should make me glad. I am confident about all of you—that what gives me joy is what gives joy to all of you.
2.4: In fact, out of much trouble and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears. My goal was not to make you sad, but that you would know how very much I love you.
2.5: Now if anyone has caused sorrow, he has not done it to me, but to all of you to some extent (not to overstate it).
2.6: This punishment inflicted on such a person by the majority is enough,
2.7: so that instead you should rather forgive and comfort him, or else such a person could be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
2.8: For that reason, I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.
2.9: In fact, this was also the purpose of my writing: I wanted to know the result of your being tested, that is, if you are obedient in all things.
2.10: If you forgive anyone anything, I do too. To be sure, if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven it in the presence of Christ for your sake,
2.11: so that Satan would not take advantage of us. We are certainly not unaware of his schemes.
2.12: When I came to Troas to proclaim the gospel of Christ and a door was opened for me by the Lord,
2.13: I had no rest in my spirit, because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said good-bye to them and went on to Macedonia.
2.14: But thanks be to God, who always causes us to triumph in Christ and reveals the fragrance of his knowledge through us in every place.
2.15: Yes, we are the fragrance of Christ for God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing.
2.16: To some we are the odor of death that is a prelude to death, to the others the fragrance of life that is a prelude to life. And who is qualified for these things?
2.17: To be sure, we are not like many who peddle the word of God for profit. Instead, in Christ we speak with sincerity in the sight of God, as men from God.

3.1: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?
3.2: You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
3.3: It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, delivered by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on stone tablets but on tablets that are hearts of flesh.
3.4: Such is the confidence we have through Christ before God.
3.5: Not that we are competent by ourselves to claim that anything comes from us; rather, our competence is from God.
3.6: He also made us competent as ministers of a new testament (not of letter, but of spirit). For the letter kills, but the spirit gives life.
3.7: If the ministry that brought death (which was engraved in letters on stone) came with glory, so that the Israelites could not look directly at the face of Moses because of the glory of his face (though it was fading),
3.8: how will the ministry of the spirit not be much more glorious?
3.9: For if the ministry that brought condemnation has glory, the ministry that brought righteousness has even more glory.
3.10: In fact, in this case, what was glorious is no longer very glorious, because of the greater glory of that which surpasses it.
3.11: Indeed, if what is fading away was glorious, how much more glorious is that which is permanent!
3.12: Therefore, since we have this kind of hope, we act with great boldness.
3.13: We are not like Moses, who put a veil over his face, so that the Israelites could not continue to look at the end of the radiance, as it was fading away.
3.14: In spite of this, their minds were hardened. Yes, up to the present day, the same veil remains when the Old Testament is read. It has not been removed because it is taken away only in Christ.
3.15: Instead, to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their hearts.
3.16: But whenever someone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
3.17: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
3.18: But all of us who reflect the Lord’s glory with an unveiled face are being transformed into his own image, from one degree of glory to another. This too is from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

4.1: Therefore, since we have this ministry as a result of the mercy shown us, we are not discouraged.
4.2: On the contrary, we have renounced shameful, underhanded methods. We do not operate in a deceitful way, and we do not distort the word of God. Instead, by proclaiming the truth clearly, we commend ourselves to everyone’s conscience in the sight of God.
4.3: But even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled among those who are perishing.
4.4: In the case of those people, the god of this age has blinded the minds of the unbelievers, to keep them from clearly seeing the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is God’s image.
4.5: Indeed, we do not preach ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.
4.6: For the God who said, “Light will shine out of darkness,” is the same one who made light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the person of Jesus Christ.
4.7: We hold this treasure in clay jars to show that its extraordinary power is from God and not from us.
4.8: We are hard pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not despairing;
4.9: persecuted, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed.
4.10: We always carry around in our body the death of the Lord Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
4.11: To be sure, while we are living we are continually being handed over to death because of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal flesh.
4.12: So then, death is working in us, but life is working in you.
4.13: Since we have that same spirit of faith, which corresponds to what is written: “I believed; therefore, I have spoken,” we also believe, and therefore we speak.
4.14: For we know that the one who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and bring us (together with you) into his presence.
4.15: In fact, all this is for your benefit, so that as grace increases, it will overflow to the glory of God, as more and more people give thanks.
4.16: Therefore we are not discouraged. But even if our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.
4.17: Yes, our momentary, light trouble produces for us an eternal weight of glory that is far beyond any comparison.
4.18: We are not focusing on what is seen, but on what is not seen. For the things that are seen are temporary, but the things that are not seen are eternal.

5.1: Now we know that if the tent that is our earthly home is destroyed, we have a building from God, an eternal home in heaven, which is not made by human hands.
5.2: In fact, the reason we groan is that we long to be clothed with our dwelling from heaven.
5.3: If we do indeed put it on, we will certainly not be found naked.
5.4: To be sure, while we are in this tent, we groan and are burdened, because we do not want to be unclothed, but to be clothed, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
5.5: Now the one who prepared us for this very purpose is God, who gave us the Spirit as the down payment.
5.6: Therefore we are always confident and know that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord,
5.7: for we walk by faith, not by sight.
5.8: But we are confident and would much prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord.
5.9: And for this reason we make it our goal to please him, whether we are at home or away.
5.10: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive what is due for what he did while in the body, whether good or bad.
5.11: So, since we know the fear of the Lord, we are trying to persuade people. Now, we are well known by God, and I hope that we are also well known in your consciences.
5.12: We are not commending ourselves to you again, but we are giving you an opportunity to boast about us, so that you have a reply for those who boast about outward appearance rather than what is in the heart.
5.13: Actually, if we were out of our minds, it was for God. If we are in our right minds, it is for you.
5.14: For the love of Christ compels us, because we came to this conclusion: One died for all; therefore, all died.
5.15: And he died for all, so that those who live would no longer live for themselves but for him, who died in their place and was raised again.
5.16: As a result, from now on, we regard no one according to the flesh. Even though we knew Christ according to the flesh, we no longer know him that way.
5.17: So then, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. The new has come!
5.18: And all these things are from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
5.19: That is, God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them. And he has entrusted to us the message of reconciliation.
5.20: Therefore, we are ambassadors for Christ, inasmuch as God is making an appeal through us. We urge you, on Christ’s behalf: Be reconciled to God.
5.21: God made him, who did not know sin, to become sin for us, so that we might become the righteousness of God in him.

6.1: As fellow workers we also urge you not to receive God’s grace in vain.
6.2:
For he says:
At a favorable time I listened to you,
and in the day of salvation I helped you.
Look, now is the favorable time! See, now is the day of salvation!
6.3: We are giving no one a reason to stumble in any way, so that our ministry will not be blamed.
6.4: Rather, in every way we show ourselves to be God’s ministers: in great endurance, in troubles, in hardships, in difficulties,
6.5: in beatings, in imprisonments, in riots, in hard work, in sleepless nights, in times of hunger;
6.6: in purity, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in sincere love,
6.7: in the word of truth, in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness on the right and on the left;
6.8: through glory and dishonor, through bad report and good report; treated as deceivers yet being honest,
6.9: treated as unknown and yet being well known; as dying, and yet look—we live; as punished yet not put to death;
6.10: as grieving yet always rejoicing; as poor yet making many rich; as having nothing yet possessing everything.
6.11: We have spoken to you openly, Corinthians. Our heart is standing wide open.
6.12: We have plenty of room for you, but you do not have room for us in your affections.
6.13: I am speaking as to my children: In exchange, open your hearts wide too.
6.14: Do not be unequally yoked together with unbelievers. For what partnership does righteousness have with lawlessness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
6.15: And what agreement does Christ have with Belial? Or what does a believer share in common with an unbeliever?
6.16:
And what mutual agreement does God’s temple have with idols? For you are the temple of the living God, just as God said:
I will live and walk among them.
I will be their God, and they will be my people.
6.17:
Therefore come out from them, and be separate, says the Lord.
Touch no unclean thing, and I will welcome you.
6.18: I will be your Father, and you will be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.

7.1: So then, since we have these promises, dear friends, let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles flesh and spirit as we seek to bring sanctification to its goal in the fear of God.
7.2: Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one. We have corrupted no one. We have taken advantage of no one.
7.3: I am not saying this to condemn you. In fact, I have said before that you are in our hearts—we died together and live together with you!
7.4: I have great confidence in you. I am very proud of you. I am filled with encouragement. I am overflowing with joy in all our trouble.
7.5: In fact, when we came to Macedonia, our flesh had no relief. Instead, we were troubled in every way—conflicts on the outside, fears on the inside.
7.6: But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us with the arrival of Titus,
7.7: and not only with his arrival, but also with the comfort he had received concerning you. He told us about your longing, your sorrow, and your serious concern for me. As a result, I rejoiced even more.
7.8: For even if I caused you sorrow with my letter, I do not regret it (even though I did regret it, for I see that my letter caused you sorrow—yet only for a little while).
7.9: Now I rejoice, not because you were made to feel sorrow, but because this sorrow resulted in repentance. Yes, you were made sorry in a godly way. So you were not harmed in any way by us.
7.10: In fact, godly sorrow produces repentance, which leads to salvation, leaving no regret. On the other hand, worldly sorrow produces death.
7.11: Yes, look what godly sorrow produced in you: what diligence, what eagerness to clear yourself, what indignation, what alarm, what longing, what zeal, what correction! In every way you proved yourselves to be pure in this matter.
7.12: So although I wrote to you, it was not because of the one who did what was wrong, or because of the one who was harmed by it. I wrote instead so that your genuine concern for us would be revealed to you in the sight of God.
7.13:
For that reason we have been comforted.
In addition to our comfort, we rejoiced a great deal more at the joy of Titus, because all of you have set his spirit at rest.
7.14: For if I made any boast to him about you, I have not been put to shame. Rather, just as everything we said to you was true, so also our boasting to Titus turned out to be true.
7.15: And his heart goes out to you even more, as he remembers the obedience of all of you (how you received him with fear and trembling).
7.16: I rejoice because I have complete confidence in you.

8.1: Now brothers, we want you to know about the grace of God that was given in the churches of Macedonia:
8.2: In a severe test of trouble, their overflowing joy and their deep poverty overflowed into an abundance of their generosity.
8.3: I testify that of their own free will they gave according to their ability, and even beyond their ability,
8.4: pleading with us with an urgent request for the gracious privilege of joining in this service to the saints.
8.5: And they did this not as we had expected, but in keeping with God’s will they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us.
8.6: As a result we urged Titus, since he had already made a beginning, to bring to completion this gracious gift on your part.
8.7: But just as you overflow in every way—in faith, in word, in knowledge, in all diligence, and in your love for us—see that you also overflow in this gracious gift.
8.8: I do not say this as a command, but to test how genuine your love is, by comparing it with the eagerness of others.
8.9: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that although he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that through his poverty you might become rich.
8.10: And I am giving advice in this matter because it is going to be helpful for you. Last year, you were not only the first to take action, but also the first to be willing.
8.11: Now bring the work to completion too, so that your eagerness to start may be matched by your completing it with what you have.
8.12: For if the eagerness is there, a gift is acceptable according to what someone has, not according to what he does not have.
8.13: Certainly, our goal is not that others take it easy while you are burdened, but that there may be equality.
8.14: At the present time, your abundance will provide what they lack, in order that their abundance will also provide what you lack—in this way there will be equality.
8.15: As it is written, “The one who gathered much did not have too much, and the one who gathered little did not have too little.”
8.16: Thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same concern I have for you,
8.17: because he accepted our encouragement and went to you eagerly, of his own free will.
8.18: We sent along with him the brother who is recognized by all the churches for his preaching of the gospel.
8.19: Not only that—but also he was elected by the churches to be our traveling companion, as we administer this gracious gift to the glory of the Lord and to show our eagerness to help.
8.20: We are trying to avoid any criticism of the way we are administering this lavish gift.
8.21: To be sure, we are taking into consideration what is proper, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of other people.
8.22: We sent along with them our brother who has often proved to us in many tests that he is eager, and now is even more eager, because of the great confidence he has in you.
8.23: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker for your benefit. Our brothers, messengers sent by the churches, are the glory of Christ.
8.24: So then, show the evidence of your love in the sight of the churches, and demonstrate why we boasted to them about you.

9.1: It is really not necessary for me to write to you about the service to the saints,
9.2: because I know your eagerness. I am boasting about it on your behalf to the Macedonians, saying that Achaia has been ready since last year. Your zeal has stirred up many of them.
9.3: But I am sending the brothers so that our boasting on your behalf will not prove to be empty in this case, but that you will be prepared just as I have been saying.
9.4: Otherwise, if any Macedonians come along with me and find you unprepared, we (to say nothing of you) would be ashamed of this confidence.
9.5: That is why I considered it necessary to urge the brothers to visit you in advance, and to arrange ahead of time the expression of praise that you previously promised, so that it may be ready as an expression of praise, not of grudging selfishness.
9.6: This is what I mean: The one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly. The one who sows generously will also reap generously.
9.7: Each one should give as he has determined in his heart, not reluctantly or under pressure, for God loves a cheerful giver.
9.8: God is able to make all grace overflow to you, so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will overflow in every good work.
9.9:
As it is written:
He scattered; he gave to the poor.
His righteousness remains forever.
9.10: And he who provides seed to the sower and bread for food will provide and multiply your seed for sowing, and will increase the harvest of your righteousness.
9.11: You will be made rich in every way so that you may be generous in every way, which produces thanksgiving to God through us.
9.12: To be sure, the administration of this service is not only making up for what is lacking among the saints, but it is also overflowing in many prayers of thanksgiving to God.
9.13: By proving yourselves in this service, many people are glorifying God, as they see the obedience shown in your confession of the gospel of Christ, and the generosity shown in your sharing with them and all people.
9.14: At the same time as they pray for you, they also express their longing for you, because of the extraordinary measure of God’s grace given to you.
9.15: Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift!

10.1: Now I myself, Paul, appeal to you by the humility and gentleness of Christ—I, who am “gentle” when I am in your presence, but “bold” toward you when I am away.
10.2: I pray that, when I arrive there, I may not have to be bold with the confidence that I expect to use in daring to confront some who think that we walk in the way the sinful flesh does.
10.3: For even though we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war in the way the sinful flesh does.
10.4: Certainly, the weapons of our warfare are not those of the flesh, but weapons made powerful by God for tearing down strongholds. We tear down thoughts
10.5: such as all arrogance that rises up against the knowledge of God, and we make every thought captive so that it is obedient to Christ.
10.6: And we are ready to punish every disobedience when your obedience is fully restored.
10.7: You are looking at things only according to the outward appearance. If anyone has convinced himself that he belongs to Christ, let him consider this about himself: We belong to Christ just as much as he does.
10.8: Indeed, even if I may boast some more about our authority, which the Lord has given for building you up and not for tearing you down, I will not be put to shame.
10.9: My purpose is not to seem as if I am trying to frighten you by my letters.
10.10: For some say, “His letters are weighty and strong, but his physical presence is weak, and his speech amounts to nothing.”
10.11: Let such a person consider this: What we are, by our word through letters when we are away, is just what we will be in our work when we are present.
10.12: To be sure, we do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some of those who speak highly of themselves. On the contrary, when they measure themselves only by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they are not wise.
10.13: But we will not boast about things that cannot be measured. Instead, we will boast according to the measure of the assignment that the God who measures things measured out to us: to reach out also as far as to you.
10.14: Indeed, we are not overdoing our boasting, as if we had not come to you. In fact, we were the first ones to come all the way to you with the gospel of Christ.
10.15: We are not boasting about things that cannot be measured, that is, in the hard work of others. But we are hoping that, as your faith grows, our assignment will be greatly increased while we are among you,
10.16: with the result that we will preach the gospel to the regions beyond you. Then we will not be boasting about what someone else has already done in his assignment.
10.17: But let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.
10.18: To be sure, it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.

11.1: I wish that you would be patient with me in regard to a little foolishness—but you are already being patient with me.
11.2: You see, I am jealous about you, with a godly jealousy, because I promised to present you as a pure virgin to one husband, Christ.
11.3: But I am afraid that somehow, just as the serpent deceived Eve with his cunning, so also your minds might be led astray from a sincere and pure devotion to Christ.
11.4: In fact, if someone comes and preaches another Jesus, whom we did not preach, or if you accept a different spirit, which you did not accept before, or a different “gospel,” which you did not welcome before, you put up with it all too well.
11.5: I do not think that I am in any way inferior to the “super-apostles.”
11.6: But even if I am an amateur in speech, yet I am not an amateur in knowledge. No, in everything we have clearly demonstrated that to you in every way.
11.7: Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself, so that you would be exalted, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?
11.8: I robbed other churches, by receiving support from them to minister to you!
11.9: And when I was with you and needed something, I did not burden anyone, because when the brothers came from Macedonia, they supplied what I needed. In every way I kept myself from ever being a burden to you, and I will continue to do so.
11.10: As the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting about me will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
11.11: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do.
11.12: But what I am doing, and will continue to do, is being done in order to cut off the opportunity of those who want an opportunity to boast that they should be considered equal to us.
11.13: In fact, such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as apostles of Christ.
11.14: And no wonder, for Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.
11.15: So it is no great surprise if his ministers also masquerade as ministers of righteousness. Their end will match their works.
11.16: I say again, no one should think that I am a fool. But if you do, then receive me as a fool, so that I may boast a little.
11.17: What I am saying when I boast so confidently is not the way the Lord speaks; rather, it is a foolish manner of speaking.
11.18: Since many are boasting as the sinful flesh does, I will also boast.
11.19: You gladly put up with fools, since you are just so wise!
11.20: In fact, you put up with it if anyone makes you his slave, robs you, takes advantage of you, looks down on you, or strikes you in the face!
11.21:
I am ashamed to say that we were too weak for that!
However bold anyone might be (I am speaking in a foolish way), I am going to be bold too.
11.22: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they Abraham’s seed? So am I.
11.23: Are they ministers of Christ? (I am speaking in a crazy way.) I am even more. I’ve done more hard work, been in prisons more often, been whipped far more, and I’ve been close to death many times.
11.24: Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.
11.25: Three times I was beaten with rods. One time I was stoned. Three times I was shipwrecked. I have spent a night and a day on the open sea.
11.26: I have often been on journeys, in danger from rivers, in danger from robbers, in danger from my own people, in danger from Gentiles, in danger in the city, in danger in the wilderness, in danger on the sea, in danger among false brothers.
11.27: I have worked hard and struggled. I’ve spent many sleepless nights. I’ve been hungry and thirsty. I’ve gone without food many times. I’ve been cold and lacked clothing.
11.28: Besides those external matters, there is the daily pressure on me of my concern for all the churches.
11.29: Who is weak without my being weak? Who falls into sin without my being distressed?
11.30: If it is necessary that I boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.
11.31: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is eternally blessed, knows that I am not lying.
11.32: In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas kept the city of Damascus on alert to arrest me,
11.33: but I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped from his hands.

12.1: I must go on boasting, although there is nothing to be gained. So I will go on to visions and revelations of the Lord.
12.2: I know a man in Christ who, fourteen years ago, was carried up to the third heaven (whether in the body, I do not know, or out of the body, I do not know—God knows).
12.3: And I know that such a man (whether in the body or out of the body, I do not know—God knows)
12.4: was carried up into Paradise and heard inexpressible words that a man cannot possibly speak.
12.5: On behalf of such a one I will boast, but on my own behalf I will not boast, except about my weaknesses.
12.6: Indeed, if I wanted to boast, I would not be a fool, because I would be speaking the truth. But I refrain from doing this, so that no one will think more highly of me than what he sees in me or hears from me.
12.7: Therefore, to keep me from becoming arrogant due to the extraordinary nature of these revelations, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan, to torment me, so that I would not become arrogant.
12.8: Three times I pleaded with the Lord about this, that he would take it away from me.
12.9: And he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, because my power is made perfect in weakness.” Therefore I will be glad to boast all the more in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may shelter me.
12.10: That is why I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties, for the sake of Christ. For whenever I am weak, then am I strong.
12.11: I have become a fool. You forced me. After all, I ought to be commended by you, because I was not inferior to the “super-apostles” in any way, even if I am nothing.
12.12: The signs of an apostle—signs and wonders and miracles—were performed among you with all perseverance.
12.13: For how were you treated worse than the other churches, except that I myself was not a burden to you? Forgive me for this wrong.
12.14: See, this is the third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be a burden to you, because I do not seek your possessions, but you. After all, the children should not have to save up for their parents, but the parents for their children.
12.15: But I will very gladly spend and be completely spent on behalf of your souls. If I love you all the more, am I to be loved that much less?
12.16: But be that as it may, I did not burden you. Oh, but I was just being crafty and using deceit to exploit you, wasn’t I!
12.17: Did I ever take advantage of you through any one of the men I sent to you?
12.18: I urged Titus to go and sent our brother with him. Surely Titus did not take any advantage of you, did he? Did we not walk in the same spirit—in the very same footprints?
12.19: Are you thinking that we are trying to defend ourselves to you all this time? We are speaking in the sight of God in Christ. Dear friends, all these words are for your strengthening.
12.20: For I am afraid that when I arrive, I may not find you as I want you to be, and that you might not find me as you want me to be. I fear that there may be quarreling, jealousy, outbursts of anger, selfishness, slander, gossip, pride, and disorder.
12.21: I fear that, when I arrive again, my God will humble me in regard to you, and I will have to grieve for many who sinned earlier and have not repented of the uncleanness, the sexual immorality, and the lewd sins they committed.

13.1: This is the third time I am coming to you. “Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.”
13.2: I have said this before, and before I arrive I am saying it again—as I did when I was present the second time, even though I am now absent—to those who sinned earlier and to all the rest: When I arrive, I will not spare you.
13.3: I say this because you are seeking proof that Christ (who is not weak toward you, but is powerful in you) is speaking in me.
13.4: To be sure, he was crucified as a result of weakness, yet he lives as a result of God’s power. Certainly, we are also weak in him, but we will live with him for your benefit, as a result of God’s power.
13.5: Examine yourselves to see if you are in the faith. Test yourselves. Or do you not know this about yourselves: that Jesus Christ is in you—unless perhaps you fail the test?
13.6: But I hope that you will recognize that we are not failing the test.
13.7: We pray to God that you may not do anything evil, not so that we may appear to have passed the test, but so that you may do what is good, even if we may seem like those who are failing to pass the test.
13.8: To be sure, we can do nothing against the truth, but only for the truth.
13.9: Yes, we rejoice whenever we are weak and you are strong. And we are praying for your complete restoration.
13.10: It is for this reason that I am writing these things while I am still absent, so that, when I am present, I may not have to deal harshly with you, using the authority that the Lord gave me for building up and not for tearing down.
13.11: Finally, brothers, rejoice. Set things in order. Be encouraged. Agree with one another. Be at peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.
13.12: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
13.13: All the saints greet you.
13.14: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

1.1: Paul, an apostle—not from men, nor through a man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead—
1.2:
and all of the brothers who are with me,
To the churches of Galatia:
1.3: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.4: He gave himself for our sins to rescue us from this present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father—
1.5: to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
1.6: I am amazed that you are so quickly deserting the one who called you in the grace of Christ, for a different gospel,
1.7: which is really not another gospel at all. There are, however, some who are trying to disturb you by perverting the gospel of Christ.
1.8: But even if we or an angel from heaven would preach any gospel other than the one we preached to you—a curse on him!
1.9: As we have said before, so I now say again: If anyone preaches to you any gospel other than the one you received—a curse on him!
1.10: Am I now seeking the favor of people or of God? Or am I striving to please people? If I were still trying to gain the approval of people, I would not be a servant of Christ.
1.11: But I want you to know, brothers, that the gospel I preached is not of human origin.
1.12: For I did not receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but I received it through a revelation from Jesus Christ.
1.13: Certainly you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how I used to persecute the church of God to an extraordinary degree and tried to destroy it.
1.14: I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries among my own people, because I was extremely zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
1.15: However, God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me by his grace, was pleased
1.16: to reveal his Son in me, so that I would preach him among the Gentiles. At that time, I did not immediately consult with flesh and blood,
1.17: and I did not go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me. Instead I went away into Arabia, and then I returned again to Damascus.
1.18: Next, after three years, I went up to Jerusalem to meet Cephas and stayed with him fifteen days.
1.19: But I saw none of the other apostles, except James, the Lord’s brother.
1.20: (Now about the things I am writing to you—look, I assure you in the presence of God that I am not lying.)
1.21: Then I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
1.22: I was still personally unknown to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.
1.23: They heard only: “The one who was once persecuting us is now preaching the faith that he once tried to destroy.”
1.24: And they were praising God for what happened to me.

2.1: Then, after fourteen years, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, also taking Titus with me.
2.2: I went up in keeping with a revelation, and I laid before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles. But I did this privately before those who were considered important, in order to make sure that I was not running—or had not run—in vain.
2.3: But Titus, who was with me, was not compelled to be circumcised, even though he is Greek.
2.4: This was an issue because of the false brothers, who slipped in under false pretenses to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus. Their goal was to make us slaves.
2.5: We refused to give in to them even for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel would continue with you.
2.6: But as for those who were considered to be important (what sort of people they once were makes no difference to me; God shows no partiality), indeed, those who were considered to be important added nothing to my gospel.
2.7: On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted with the gospel for the uncircumcised, just as Peter was entrusted with the gospel for the circumcised.
2.8: For God, who worked effectively in Peter to serve as an apostle to the circumcised, also worked effectively in me to serve as an apostle to the Gentiles.
2.9: And because James, Cephas, and John, who were considered to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given to me, they gave Barnabas and me the right hand of fellowship. They agreed that we were to go to the Gentiles and they to the circumcised.
2.10: The only thing they asked was that we remember the poor, the very thing that I was also eager to do.
2.11: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he was clearly wrong.
2.12: For before some people came from James, he ate with the Gentiles. But when those people came, he drew back and separated himself, because he feared those from the circumcision group.
2.13: And the rest of the Jews joined him in his hypocrisy, with the result that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.
2.14: But when I saw that they were not acting according to the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of all of them, “If you, a Jew, live like the Gentiles and not like the Jews, why do you compel the Gentiles to live like the Jews?”
2.15: “We are Jews by birth and not Gentile sinners.
2.16: We know that a person is not justified by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ. So we also believed in Christ Jesus that we might be justified by faith in Christ and not by the works of the law, because no one will be justified by the works of the law.
2.17: But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves were also found to be sinners, then is Christ a servant of sin? Certainly not!
2.18: “In fact, if I build up again those things that I destroyed, I bring on myself the judgment of being a lawbreaker.
2.19: Indeed, through the law I died to the law that I might live for God.
2.20: I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I am now living in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
2.21: I do not regard the grace of God as nothing. As a matter of fact, if righteousness is through the law, then Christ died for nothing!”

3.1: O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you? Before your very eyes Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed as crucified.
3.2: I just want to learn this from you: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by believing what you heard?
3.3: Are you so foolish? Having begun by the Spirit, are you now trying to reach the goal by the flesh?
3.4: Did you experience so many things for nothing, if it were indeed for nothing?
3.5: So then, does the one who supplies the Spirit to you and works miracles among you, do it by the works of the law? Or does he do it by your believing what you hear—
3.6: in the same way as Abraham “believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness”?
3.7: Understand, then, that those who believe are the children of Abraham.
3.8: Foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, Scripture proclaimed the gospel in advance to Abraham, saying, “In you, all nations will be blessed.”
3.9: So then, those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
3.10: In fact, those who rely on the works of the law are under a curse. For it is written, “Cursed is everyone who does not continue to do everything written in the book of the law.”
3.11: Clearly no one is declared righteous before God by the law, because “The righteous will live by faith.”
3.12: The law does not say “by faith.” Instead it says, “The one who does these things will live by them.”
3.13: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. As it is written, “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.”
3.14: He redeemed us in order that the blessing of Abraham would come to the Gentiles through Christ Jesus, so that we would receive the promised Spirit through faith.
3.15: Brothers, I am speaking in human terms. When someone has established a last will and testament, no one nullifies it or adds to it.
3.16: The promises God spoke referred to Abraham and to his seed. It doesn’t say, “And to seeds,” as if it were referring to many, but, as referring to one, “And to your seed,” who is Christ.
3.17: What I am saying is this: The law, which came into being 430 years after the covenant established earlier by God in Christ, does not annul that covenant, with the result that it invalidates the promise.
3.18: In fact, if the inheritance is by the law, it is no longer by the promise. But God graciously gave it to Abraham by a promise.
3.19: Then what about the law? It was added for the purpose of revealing transgressions, until the Seed to whom the promise referred had come. It was transmitted through angels by the hand of a mediator.
3.20: Now a mediator is not needed for one party, but God is one.
3.21: Then is the law against the promises of God? Certainly not! For if there had been a law given that could give life, certainly righteousness would have been derived from the law.
3.22: But Scripture imprisoned all things under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ would be given to those who believe.
3.23: But before this faith came, we were held in custody under the law, imprisoned until the coming faith was revealed.
3.24: So the law was our chaperone until Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
3.25: But now that this faith has come, we are no longer under a chaperone.
3.26: In fact, you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
3.27: Indeed, as many of you as were baptized into Christ have been clothed with Christ.
3.28: There is not Jew or Greek, slave or free, male or female, for you are all one and the same in Christ Jesus.
3.29: And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s descendants and heirs according to the promise.

4.1: What I am saying is this: As long as the heir is a young child, he is no different from a slave. Although he is owner of everything,
4.2: he is still under guardians and managers until the day set by his father.
4.3: So also, when we were younger children, we were enslaved under the basic principles of the world.
4.4: But when the set time had fully come, God sent his Son to be born of a woman, so that he would be born under the law,
4.5: in order to redeem those under the law, so that we would be adopted as sons.
4.6: And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts to shout, “Abba, Father!”
4.7: So you are no longer a slave, but a son. And if you are a son, then you are also an heir of God through Christ.
4.8: Formerly, when you did not know God, you were slaves to those who by nature are not gods.
4.9: But now that you know God, or rather are known by God, why are you turning back again to the basic principles that are weak and miserable? Do you want to be enslaved by them all over again?
4.10: You carefully observe days, months, seasons, and years.
4.11: I am fearful about you, that somehow my labor for you was wasted.
4.12: I beg you, brothers, become like me, for I also became like you. You did me no harm.
4.13: You know that, because of a weakness of the flesh, I preached the gospel to you the first time.
4.14: And you did not despise or disdain the test my flesh gave you. Instead, you welcomed me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
4.15: So where is this blessed attitude of yours now? Yes, I can say for a fact that, if it were possible, you would have plucked out your eyes and given them to me.
4.16: So then, have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?
4.17: Those people are eager to win you over, but not in a good way. Rather, they want to alienate you, so that you will be eager for them.
4.18: But it is always a good thing to have someone eager in a good way—not just when I am present with you.
4.19: My children, I am suffering birth pains for you again until Christ is formed in you.
4.20: I wish I were present with you now and could change my tone, because I am perplexed about you.
4.21: Tell me, you who want to be under the law, are you really listening to the law?
4.22: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman, and one by the free woman.
4.23: However, the son by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, but the son by the free woman was born through a promise.
4.24: These things can be used as an illustration; namely, the women are two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing children into slavery. This is Hagar.
4.25: You see, this Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and she corresponds to present-day Jerusalem, because Jerusalem is in slavery along with her children.
4.26: But the Jerusalem that is above is free. She is our mother.
4.27:
For it is written:
Rejoice, barren woman who does not give birth. Break forth and shout for joy, woman who does not suffer birth pains, because the barren woman has more children than does the woman who has a husband.
4.28: Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of the promise.
4.29: But just as back then the one who was born according to the flesh persecuted the one who was born according to the Spirit, so this is also the case now.
4.30: But what does the Scripture say? “Throw out the slave woman and her son, because the son of the slave woman will certainly not receive the inheritance with the son of the free woman.”
4.31: For this same reason, brothers, we are not children of a slave woman, but of the free woman.

5.1: It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not allow anyone to put the yoke of slavery on you again.
5.2: Look, I, Paul, tell you that if you allow yourselves to be circumcised, Christ will be of no benefit to you.
5.3: I testify again to every man who allows himself to be circumcised that he is obligated to do the whole law.
5.4: You who are trying to be declared righteous by the law are completely separated from Christ. You have fallen from grace.
5.5: Indeed, through the Spirit, we by faith are eagerly waiting for the sure hope of righteousness.
5.6: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision matters. Rather, it is faith working through love that matters.
5.7: You were running well! Who cut in on you, so that you are no longer persuaded by the truth?
5.8: This persuasion is not from the one who calls you.
5.9: A little yeast works through the whole batch.
5.10: I am confident in the Lord that you will have no other opinion than this. But the one who is trying to disturb you will pay the penalty, whoever he is.
5.11: Brothers, if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? Then the offense of the cross has been abolished.
5.12: If only those who are upsetting you would also cut themselves off!
5.13: After all, brothers, you were called to freedom. Only do not use your freedom as a starting point for your sinful flesh. Rather, serve one another through love.
5.14: In fact, the whole law is summed up in this one statement: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
5.15: But if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out that you are not consumed by one another.
5.16: What I am saying is this: Walk by the spirit, and you will not carry out what the sinful flesh desires.
5.17: For the sinful flesh desires what is contrary to the spirit, and the spirit what is contrary to the sinful flesh. In fact, these two continually oppose one another, so that you do not continue to do these things you want to do.
5.18: But if you are led by the spirit, you are not under the control of the law.
5.19: Now the works of the sinful flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, complete lack of restraint,
5.20: idolatry, sorcery, hatred, discord, jealousy, outbursts of anger, selfish ambition, dissensions, heresies,
5.21: envy, murders, drunkenness, orgies, and things similar to these. I warn you, just as I also warned you before, that those who continue to do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
5.22: But the fruit of the spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
5.23: gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
5.24: Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the sinful flesh with its passions and desires.
5.25: If we live by the spirit, let us also walk in step with it.
5.26: Let us not become conceited, provoking one another and envying one another.

6.1: Brothers, if a person is caught in some trespass, you who are spiritual should restore such a person in a spirit of humility, carefully watching yourself so that you are not also tempted.
6.2: Bear one another’s burdens, and in this way fulfill the law of Christ.
6.3: For if someone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
6.4: Let each person test his own work, and then he will take pride in regard to himself and not his neighbor.
6.5: For each man will bear his own burden.
6.6: Let the one who is taught the word share all good things with his teacher.
6.7: Do not be deceived. God is not mocked. To be sure, whatever a man sows, he will also reap.
6.8: Indeed, the one who sows for his own sinful flesh will reap destruction from the sinful flesh. But the one who sows for the spirit will reap eternal life from the spirit.
6.9: Let us not become weary of doing good, because at the appointed time we will reap, if we do not give up.
6.10: So then, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people, and especially to those who belong to the household of faith.
6.11: See what large letters I am writing to you with my own hand.
6.12: Those who want to look good in the flesh are the ones who are trying to compel you to be circumcised. Their only reason is so that they are not persecuted for the cross of Christ.
6.13: As a matter of fact, those who are circumcised do not keep the law themselves. But they want to have you circumcised, so that they can boast about your flesh.
6.14: But far be it from me to boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me and I to the world.
6.15: In fact, in Christ Jesus circumcision or uncircumcision does not matter. What matters is being a new creation.
6.16: Peace and mercy on those who follow this rule, namely, on the Israel of God.
6.17: Finally, let no one cause me any trouble, because I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus on my body.
6.18: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.

1.1:
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God,
To the saints who are in Ephesus, who are believers in Christ Jesus:
1.2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places.
1.4: He did this when he chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world, so that we would be holy and blameless in his sight. In love
1.5: he predestined us to be adopted as his sons through Jesus Christ. He did this in accordance with the good purpose of his will,
1.6: and for the praise of his glorious grace, which he has graciously given us in the one he loves.
1.7: In him we also have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, in keeping with the riches of his grace,
1.8: which he lavished on us in all wisdom and insight.
1.9: He made known to us the mystery of his will in keeping with his good purpose, which he planned in Christ.
1.10: This was to be carried out when the time had fully come, in order to bring all things together in Christ, things in heaven and things on earth.
1.11: In him we have also obtained an inheritance, because we were predestined according to the plan of him who works out everything in keeping with the purpose of his will.
1.12: He did this so that his glory would be praised as a result of us, who were the first to hope in Christ.
1.13: In him, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and in him, when you also believed, you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit.
1.14: He is the down payment of our inheritance until the redemption of God’s own possession, so that his glory would be praised.
1.15: This is why, ever since I heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints,
1.16: I never stop giving thanks for you, remembering you in my prayers.
1.17: I keep praying that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father, will give you the Spirit of wisdom and revelation in knowing Christ fully.
1.18: I pray that the eyes of your heart may be enlightened, so that you may know the hope to which he has called you, just how rich his glorious inheritance among the saints is,
1.19: and just how surpassingly great his power is for us who believe.
1.20: It is as great as the working of his mighty strength, which God worked in Christ when he raised him from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly places,
1.21: far above all rule, authority, power, and dominion, and above every name that is given, not only in this age but also in the one to come.
1.22: God also placed all things under his feet and made him head over everything for the church.
1.23: The church is his body, the fullness of him who fills everything in every way.

2.1: You were dead in your trespasses and sins,
2.2: in which you formerly walked when you followed the ways of this present world. You were following the ruler of the domain of the air, the spirit now at work in the people who disobey.
2.3: Formerly, we all lived among them in the passions of our sinful flesh, as we carried out the desires of the sinful flesh and its thoughts. Like all the others, we were by nature objects of God’s wrath.
2.4: But God, because he is rich in mercy, because of the great love with which he loved us,
2.5: made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in trespasses. It is by grace you have been saved!
2.6: He also raised us up with Christ and seated us with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus.
2.7: He did this so that, in the coming ages, he might demonstrate the surpassing riches of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus.
2.8: Indeed, it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God—
2.9: not by works, so that no one can boast.
2.10: For we are God’s workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared in advance so that we would walk in them.
2.11: Therefore, remember that at one time, you Gentiles in the flesh—the ones who are called “uncircumcised” by those called “the circumcised” (which is performed physically by human hands)—
2.12: remember that at that time you were separated from Christ, excluded from the citizenship of Israel, and foreigners to the covenants of the promise. You were without hope and without God in the world.
2.13: But now in Christ Jesus, you who once were far away have been brought near by the blood of Christ.
2.14: For he himself is our peace. He made the two groups one by destroying the wall of hostility that divided them
2.15: when he abolished the law of commandments and regulations in his flesh. He did this to create in himself one new person out of the two, in this way making peace.
2.16: And he did this to reconcile both to God in one body through the cross by putting the hostility to death on it.
2.17: He also came and preached peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near.
2.18: For through him we both have access to the Father by one Spirit.
2.19: So then, you are no longer foreigners and strangers, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and members of God’s household.
2.20: You have been built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the Cornerstone.
2.21: In him the whole building is joined together and grows into a holy temple in the Lord.
2.22: In him you too are being built together into a dwelling place for God by the Spirit.

3.1: For this reason, I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of you Gentiles—
3.2: Surely you have heard of the administration of God’s grace given to me for you,
3.3: namely, that the mystery was made known to me by revelation (as I have already written briefly).
3.4: When you read this, you will be able to understand my insight into the mystery of Christ.
3.5: This mystery was not made known to people in past generations as it has now been revealed by the Spirit to his holy apostles and prophets.
3.6: This mystery is that in Christ Jesus the Gentiles are fellow heirs, members of the same body, and people who also share in the promise through the gospel.
3.7: I became a servant of this gospel, in keeping with the gift of God’s grace that was given to me by the working of his power.
3.8: To me—even though I am the very least of all the saints—was given this grace: to preach to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ
3.9: and to enlighten everyone about the administration of this mystery. In past ages this mystery remained hidden in God, who created all things.
